latestRelease.notes:
# Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (v2026.8.13)

**Release Date:** August 13, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~656 PRs merged since v0.20.0 into a stable tagged release for downstream consumers (Docker images, hosted deployments, and anyone installing from the latest tag).

---

## About this release

Since v0.20.0 (August 3), this window landed **1,444 commits** across **~656 merged PRs**, touching **2,172 files** (+233,872 / −75,244), and closed **~481 issues**. It is a broad stabilization-and-fixes rollup spanning the desktop app, gateway platforms, installers, tool system, and provider catalogs.

**Full curated release notes for this window will ship with v0.21.0**, which will document everything from v0.20.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- Existing installs: `hermes update`
- Fresh install: see the installer one-liner in the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent#readme)

**Full Changelog**: [v2026.8.3...v2026.8.13](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v2026.8.3...v2026.8.13)

signals.title: vision_analyze fails with kimi-coding provider: native vision fast path blocked
signals.text:
## Bug Description When using kimi-coding provider with model kimi-for-coding (Kimi K2.6), the vision_analyze tool fails with: 
Error analyzing image: No LLM provider configured for task=vision provider=auto. Run: hermes setup
This happens even though Kimi K2.6 supports multimodal/vision natively. ## Root Cause Analysis Two issues chain together: ### 1. Provider not in native vision allow-list _supports_media_in_tool_results() in tools/vision_tools.py does not include kimi-coding, so the native fast path is skipped. ### 2. Config model name not resolvable in models.dev Config uses friendly name kimi-for-coding, but models.dev cache stores the canonical ID k2p6. _find_model_entry() cannot bridge this gap, so get_model_capabilities() returns None. This causes decide_image_input_mode() to fall back to 'text' mode, which triggers the legacy auxiliary-LLM path. Since no auxiliary vision provider is configured, it fails. ## Reproduction Steps 1. Set config: model.default: kimi-for-coding, model.provider: kimi-coding 2. Send an image to the agent 3. Agent calls vision_analyze 4. Error: No LLM provider configured for task=vision ## Expected Behavior vision_analyze should use the native fast path, returning a multimodal tool-result envelope with the base64-encoded image, allowing the main model (Kimi K2.6) to see the pixels directly. ## Environment - Provider: kimi-coding - Model: kimi-for-coding (Kimi K2.6) - Hermes version: main @ e85592591 ## Proposed Fix 1. Add kimi-coding, kimi-coding-cn, kimi, moonshot to _supports_media_in_tool_results() 2. Add _MODEL_ALIASES mapping in _find_model_entry() to bridge friendly config names to canonical models.dev IDs --- I have a branch ready with the fix.

signals.title: [UX] Enable mouse support (cursor positioning, scrolling) with config toggle
signals.text: ## Summary Mouse support is explicitly disabled in the prompt_toolkit Application: `cli.py:1755`: ```python mouse_support=False, ``` This means users cannot: - Click to position the cursor in the input area - Select text with the mouse - Scroll with the mouse wheel (within prompt_toolkit) ## Suggested fix 1. Flip to `mouse_support=True` as the default 2. Add a `tui.mouse_support` config toggle as an escape hatch for terminals where mouse capture causes issues (tmux, screen, some SSH setups) ```python mouse_support=self.config.get("tui", {}).get("mouse_support", True), ``` ## Risk Low. Some terminal multiplexers (tmux, screen) may behave oddly with mouse capture enabled. The config toggle provides an escape hatch. Most modern terminals handle this fine. ## Impact - **Severity**: High — basic expected interaction pattern - **Effort**: Tiny — one boolean flip + optional config key ## Ref UX audit item #10.

signals.title: [Feature]: Desktop surface parity with Web Dashboard (phased admin + plugins + kanban)
signals.text: ## Summary Bring the management and multi-agent surfaces that today live primarily in `hermes dashboard` into **Hermes Desktop**, so Desktop can be a single day-to-day app without forcing a browser switch for ops work. This is **not** a request to delete the web dashboard or embed a full browser tab as the only solution. Prefer native Desktop UX (or a shared React package) on top of the same backend APIs Desktop already can reach. ## Problem Desktop is chat-first; Web Dashboard is the machine-level admin panel (config, keys, channels, MCP, webhooks, logs/analytics, kanban plugin, themes, dashboard plugins). Users who live in Desktop still bounce to `http://127.0.0.1:9119` for many tasks. That split feels like two products on one install. ### Related prior art (children / blockers, not competitors) - Kanban in Desktop: #41222 (#50173 / #48159 duplicates) - Dashboard plugin loader on Desktop: #49363 - Hybrid HTTP admin path: #51065 (closed as `implemented-on-main` — use as base) - Theme/skin sync: #50190 - Boardstate Desktop phase 2: #66413 - Community workspace integration: #41553 - Unified quota/usage center (Desktop + Dashboard): #59425 ## Goals 1. **One primary shell for daily use:** Desktop chat + core admin without browser. 2. **One backend contract:** reuse dashboard HTTP/WS APIs; no second source of truth. 3. **Plugin parity path:** dashboard plugins (incl. kanban) loadable in Desktop via the same manifest/SDK contract (#49363), or officially vendored native panes. 4. **Keep web dashboard** for remote/headless/server ops and thin clients. ## Non-goals - Replacing Desktop’s native chat with the dashboard Chat/TUI pane. - Forcing all admin only on Desktop (web remains supported). - Pixel-identical UI; functional parity first. ## Proposed phases ### Phase 0 — Inventory & API map - Matrix of web pages vs Desktop panes vs API endpoints. - Confirm what #51065 already unlocked on current `main`. ### Phase 1 — Highest-friction admin in Desktop Native or shared panes for: - Config (schema form) - API keys / secrets - MCP servers - Messaging channels - Skills full lifecycle (search/install/publish if web has it) - Logs + basic analytics/usage ### Phase 2 — Multi-agent surfaces - Kanban board panel (#41222) — full visual board or embed shared kanban plugin UI - Live agents / subagent tree parity where still missing - Boardstate Desktop phase (#66413) ### Phase 3 — Extensibility & polish - Dashboard plugin runtime in Desktop (#49363) - Theme/font/skin sync with web (#50190) — optional but reduces “two products” feel - Deep links: Desktop → specific admin route; web → open session in Desktop ## Suggested architecture options (pick one in implementation) | Option | Approach | |--------|----------| | **A** | Shared UI package (`@hermes/dashboard-ui` routes mounted in Electron + web) | | **B** | Desktop plugin host consuming web dashboard plugin manifests unchanged | | **C** | Native Desktop panes calling the same HTTP APIs (no shared React) | Prefer **A** or **B** for kanban/plugins to avoid permanent dual maintenance. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Desktop user can complete config, keys, MCP, channels, and skills install without opening a browser - [ ] Kanban create/list/move/comment works from Desktop against the same `kanban.db` / board APIs as web - [ ] At least one real dashboard plugin loads in Desktop unchanged, **or** is officially re-hosted as a Desktop pane with feature parity - [ ] No second write path that can diverge profile / `HERMES_HOME` state - [ ] Web dashboard remains fully usable for remote/headless setups - [ ] Docs: “Desktop vs Web” matrix updated ## Motivation (user context) I run Hermes on Windows with both Desktop and `hermes dashboard`. Config/session/kanban data is already shared via the same `HERMES_HOME`, but the **admin and multi-agent UIs are not**. Opening the browser just for Kanban, MCP, channels, or full config breaks flow when Desktop is the primary shell. Happy to refine scope or split phases if maintainers prefer thinner issues under this tracker.

signals.title: [Bug]: Desktop composer draft is cleared when a todo task completes
signals.text: ## Bug description In Hermes Desktop on Windows, an unsent message being typed in the composer can disappear when the running agent completes a task-list (`todo`) item. This is data loss: the user can lose several minutes of typed text. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open Hermes Desktop on Windows. 2. Start an agent task that uses the `todo` tool and will mark a task as completed. 3. While the agent is still running, type a multi-sentence message in the Desktop composer, but do not send it. 4. When the agent finishes a task-list item / the todo status updates to completed, inspect the composer. ## Expected behavior The composer draft must survive all agent-status and todo-list updates. Only an explicit send, user clear action, or deliberate session change should clear typed text. ## Actual behavior The entire unsent composer draft is cleared when the task-list item completes. The user reports losing up to about five minutes of typing. ## Impact High UX impact because this silently destroys user-authored text during normal agent execution. ## Environment - Platform: Hermes Desktop - OS: Windows 11 Home (build 26200 / 25H2) - Hermes Agent: `v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)` - Upstream revision: `3a2b3329` - Python: `3.11.15` ## Notes This is currently a user-reported Desktop behavior. It should be investigated around composer state ownership/remounting when `todo` status events update the status/task-list UI.

signals.title: Desktop restart reaps the live gateway but never relaunches it (WeChat/QQ go silent) — regression
signals.text: ## Summary On Windows (Hermes 0.20.0, desktop app), **every desktop-app restart force-kills the running messaging gateway and never relaunches it**. WeChat (iLink), QQ bot and Telegram go completely silent until the gateway is manually restarted. This is a regression: before this version, the old gateway survived desktop restarts (reparented), so messaging stayed online. ## Root cause In `hermes_cli/web_server.py`, when the desktop backend starts (`HERMES_DESKTOP=1`), it calls `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` before boot, with the comment *"Before forking a fresh gateway, reap any orphan left by a previous serve session... (#77276)"*. However: 1. `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` → `find_gateway_pids()` → `_scan_gateway_pids()` matches **any** process whose command line looks like `hermes_cli.main gateway run` (`looks_like_gateway_command_line`), including gateways started by the Windows scheduled task (`Hermes_Gateway`) or manually via `hermes gateway run`. It writes the planned-stop marker, sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILLs survivors after 5s. 2. The comment says "before **forking** a fresh gateway", but `hermes serve` does **not** spawn a gateway at all (per the same file: *"The Desktop backend is spawned as `hermes serve` — it runs neither the interactive CLI nor the messaging gateway"*). Gateway startup is delegated to external mechanisms (the login scheduled task, the update flow, or a manual `hermes gateway run`). 3. Result: **every desktop restart reaps the live gateway with no successor**. The gateway exits uncleanly (`gateway-exit-diag.log`: *"exited UNCLEANLY (no exit path ran — SIGKILL / OOM / VM death)"*), and `.gateway-planned-stop.json` is left behind. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Start the gateway (login scheduled task or `hermes gateway run`). WeChat/QQ/Telegram connect fine. 2. Close and reopen the Hermes desktop app. 3. The gateway process is gone (no exit logs; killed externally). Messages sent via WeChat/QQ get no reply until the gateway is manually restarted. Secondary symptom: the third-party skin plugin (`skin-studio`) re-asserts the configured skin on boot but only retries for ~2.5 s, while the desktop backend takes longer to become ready — so after a desktop restart the skin silently falls back to default until manually re-applied. Same class of "desktop restart breaks things that depend on the gateway/backend". ## Suggested fixes - **Option A**: when the desktop reap kills a live gateway, the desktop backend (or Electron main) should spawn a replacement immediately after reap (complete the "fork a fresh gateway" the comment promises). - **Option B**: only reap gateways that are truly unsupervised (no `gateway.pid` record / not the login scheduled-task instance), instead of every process matching `gateway run`. - **Option C**: add a config switch (e.g. `gateway.reap_on_desktop_start: false`) so users who manage the gateway externally (scheduled task / systemd / manual) can opt out. ## Workaround (user side) A 2-minute Hermes-internal cron job that checks for the gateway process and relaunches it detached with the full environment. Works, but leaves a gap and depends on the desktop backend's own cron scheduler. ## Environment - Windows 11, Hermes 0.20.0 (commit 33f8e96a72), desktop app, Python 3.12 - Platforms: WeChat (iLink), QQ Bot, Telegram (via local proxy) - `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` serve backend; gateway launched via `python.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run`

signals.title: [Bug]: Hermes opening chrome link for local browser searching
signals.text: ### Bug Description In the latest version of Hermes, when I instruct for a web search with a prompt that includes. `search the web and research extra information` during the prompt processing it shows... ``` The browser needs your authorization. Chrome should have opened chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging — please: 1. Tick "Allow remote debugging for this browser instance" 2. Click "Allow" on the popup ``` If I open chrome and use the chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging URL I can enable remote debugging. signals.title: [Bug]: Cron delivery silently dropped and react opaque-id passthrough gone for targets resolve_send_target can't resolve
signals.text: ### Bug Description Since d409f6748 ("feat(platforms): add typed plugin send paths"), cron job delivery is silently dropped for targets that resolve_send_target can't resolve, and send_message's react/unreact actions reject platform-native ids they used to pass through. Before that commit, `_resolve_single_delivery_target` in `cron/scheduler.py` fell back to the raw target string whenever the target wasn't parser-explicit, and swallowed directory-resolution failures. The raw id went to the adapter, which validated it. After the commit it calls `resolve_send_target`, and on any resolution error it logs a warning and returns None, which the caller treats the same as `deliver: local`. The job runs, the output goes nowhere, and the only trace is a warning in the scheduler log. The react handler had the same lane removed. The old code was explicit about it, comment included: ```python # Opaque platform-native ids (e.g. photon space GUIDs like # 'any;-;+1555...') match no parser pattern and no directory # entry — pass them through verbatim; the adapter validates. chat_id = resolved or target_ref ``` The compensating `_PHOTON_DM_GUID_RE` added later only covers photon DM GUIDs (`any;-;+digits`). Group GUIDs (`iMessage;+;chat...`) and every other platform's native shapes still bounce. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a cron job with a deliver target the channel directory doesn't know, for example `deliver: "telegram:ops-room"` on a fresh install where the directory hasn't been populated, or a photon group GUID like `deliver: "photon:iMessage;+;chat527148912345"` 2. Let the job fire 3. The scheduler logs `Invalid cron delivery target ...` and the job output is not delivered anywhere For react: `send_message(action="react", target="photon:iMessage;+;chat527148912345", ...)` returns a resolution error instead of reaching the adapter. ### Expected Behavior The pre-d409f6748 behavior on these surfaces: an unresolved target passes through verbatim and the adapter validates it. These are stored jobs and native message ids, there's no model in the loop to read the error and pick a different target. ### Actual Behavior Cron: warning log, delivery skipped, output lost. React: tool error, reaction never attempted. ### Affected Component Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.), Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp) ### Debug Report Not applicable, found by reviewing the d409f6748 diff against the prior code and confirmed by reading both paths on current main (`cron/scheduler.py` around line 1371, `tools/send_message_tool.py` `_handle_react` and the tail of `resolve_send_target`). No live deployment involved. ### Operating System Windows 11 (repro is platform-independent) ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) `resolve_send_target` was written for the model-facing send surface, where erroring on an unresolved target is good UX (the model gets a hint, calls `action='list'`, retries). Cron and react were switched onto it wholesale, but they have no retry loop, so the strictness converts to silent data loss. The old verbatim fallback wasn't an accident on those surfaces, the react comment documented it. ### Proposed Fix (optional) Add an opt-in `pass_unresolved_references` flag to `resolve_send_target`, used only by cron and react: unresolved targets on built-in platforms, or on plugin platforms that declare no parser, pass through verbatim (validator still runs). Plugin platforms that declare a parser stay strict everywhere, since the parser being authoritative is the point of the typed-send-path work. The model-facing default is unchanged. PR incoming. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: [Feature]: Route file:// links / raw local paths through #media: in Desktop chat (currently rendered as [blocked])
signals.text: ### Environment Windows 11, Hermes Desktop app (packaged build), streamdown 2.5.0 / @assistant-ui/react-streamdown 0.3.5 ### Problem When the agent emits a markdown link pointing at a local file, e.g. ```markdown [open the report](file:///C:/Users/PC/Desktop/report.md) ``` the chat renders it as `open the report [blocked]` — the link is replaced by the text `[blocked]` and is not clickable at all. Root cause: `harden-react-markdown` (bundled inside streamdown) hard-blocks the `file:` protocol. Its allowlist is `https/http/irc/ircs/mailto/xmpp/blob` and its deny set includes `file:`, `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`. Per the package's own Security Note, `file:` is always blocked even with `allowedProtocols={['*']}` — there is no configuration escape hatch. This is a UX dead-end for a desktop app whose whole point is dealing with local files: the main process already knows how to open local files (`electron/main.ts` `openExternalUrl` → `shell.openPath`), so the capability exists — only the render layer kills the link before it can be clicked. ### Related - #38786 — generated local images rendered as `[Image blocked: ...]`; fixed by routing raw local paths through the `#media:<encoded-path>` protocol. Same root cause, same fix pattern. ### Expected behavior A `file://` link (or a raw Windows local path such as `C:\Users\...`) emitted by the agent should render as a clickable link/card that opens the local file with the OS default app via `shell.openPath` — e.g. by auto-converting it to `#media:<encodeURIComponent(path)>` in the markdown preprocess step, or by letting the markdown link component handle the `file:` protocol through the media path. ### Additional findings from debugging this (for whoever implements it) `#media:` already works end-user-side, with two format traps: 1. The href must start with `#media:` exactly. A leading slash (`/#media:...`) does not match `mediaPathFromMarkdownHref` (`startsWith('#media:')`), silently degrades to a plain link, and clicking it turns into SPA navigation — desktop.log then shows `Error invoking remote method 'hermes:openExternal': Error: Invalid external URL (file:///...index.html#/...)`. Users perceive this as "opens C:\ root". 2. The encoded path should be forward-slash form `/C:/Users/...` so `mediaExternalUrl` concatenates a valid `file:///C:/...` URL. Backslash form produces an invalid `file://C:\...` URL. Also: when `shell.openPath` fails (e.g. file extension association hijacked by a third-party app), the fallback `showItemInFolder` reveals the drive root rather than the file's folder, which is confusing. A clearer fallback (or an error toast naming the file) would help. This is a UX enhancement — `#media:` links hand-authored today work; the request is for `file://` links to work (or degrade gracefully) instead of rendering `[blocked]`.

signals.title: False positive: "TERMINAL_CWD deprecated" warning on every gateway start (env var, not .env)
signals.text: ## Summary Hermes shows a deprecation warning on every start even though the user **never set** `TERMINAL_CWD` in `~/.hermes/.env` (the only occurrence is a commented-out `# TERMINAL_CWD=.`): ``` ⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected: ⚠ TERMINAL_CWD=/path/to/project found in .env — this is deprecated. Move to config.yaml instead: terminal: cwd: /your/project/path Then remove the old entries from ~/.hermes/.env ``` ## Root cause (traced in source) 1. `cli.py:7706` (`_restore_session_cwd`) sets `os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"]` when a session with a recorded cwd is resumed (`/resume`, `--resume`, continuing an old session). The env var then **outlives the session** and sticks to the shell/process env. 2. `gateway/run.py:2395` calls `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()`, which reads `os.environ.get("TERMINAL_CWD")` (config.py:2151) — i.e. **process env**, not the .env **file**. 3. `doctor.py:436-437` explicitly documents the intended behavior: deprecated env vars should be *"checked in the .env file, not process env, so config→env bridges like terminal.cwd → TERMINAL_CWD do not false-positive."* So `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` contradicts doctor.py: it checks process env, which the config bridge / session-restore populates legitimately, and reports a user-facing deprecation warning that is a false positive. ## Repro - Any session whose process env already contains `TERMINAL_CWD` (e.g. after resuming a session created in a project dir). - `env -u TERMINAL_CWD hermes chat -q ok` suppresses the warning; with `TERMINAL_CWD` set it appears. Verified: with env set → 1 warning, without → 0. ## Expected `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` should read the **.env file** (like `doctor.py` does) instead of `os.environ`, so a launch-artifact / config-bridge value never triggers a user-facing "you have a deprecated setting" warning. At minimum, skip the warning when `terminal.cwd` in config.yaml is non-explicit (".") and the env value matches the session-restore path. ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13) - OS: Linux Mint - Source: cli

signals.title: [Bug]: api_server wake self-POSTs async-delegation completion as a user turn after parent complete
signals.text: ### Bug Description ### Observed on gateway platform=api_server (WebUI /v1/runs + X-Hermes-Session-Id). **Not** Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp — those use MessageEvent(internal=True) push, a different wake path. On the API server path, a background delegate_task completion is delivered by self-POSTing /v1/chat/completions with role=user. That starts a new agent turn. If the parent has already ended (finish_reason=stop, SSE event.complete) and is waiting for a human follow-up (skill/convention “please confirm before continuing”), this internal wake is indistinguishable from the user saying “continue.” There is no runtime Confirm gate, so the model proceeds on its own (writes, skips the confirm UI, etc.). This is a class of problem on api_server, not a single skill. Messaging auto-resume on idle is a different contract; here event.complete means the client owns the next turn. Not: - A regression of the session-turn-lock work ([#84876](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/84876)). The lock only serializes; after complete it is free, so the wake runs as a second turn and the bug is easier to see. - The runtime parsing wake as “user clicked Confirm.” There is no Confirm primitive. - The word act being a magic switch. It is prompt pressure; BATCH COMPLETE as a user message is enough to continue. - Subagent dispatch/execution being broken. Both children completed normally. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run the gateway with the API server enabled (WebUI / HQ / any client using X-Hermes-Session-Id). 2. POST /v1/runs on a session whose prompt causes the parent to: > dispatch one or more background delegate_tasks, then > stop and ask the user to confirm before any further writes / next stage. 3. Wait until the parent turn ends: SSE event.complete, finish_reason=stop, last assistant text is a confirmation request. 4. Do not send a user message. Wait for a background child to finish (or for a wake that arrived during the parent turn and was queued until complete). 5. Watch the same session_id for a second turn with no client request. Minimal shape: any workflow that (a) uses async subagents and (b) ends a turn waiting for a human. A confirm-gated skill is sufficient; the skill is not the bug. ### Expected Behavior After the parent event.complete, the session stays idle until the client sends the next message. Background completion should be persisted on the session (or attached to that next client turn as context). It must not be treated as a new user prompt, and must not be worded as permission to pass a pending human gate. Telegram/Discord-style idle auto-resume is unchanged; this is the non-push api_server self-POST path. ### Actual Behavior Observed on session 49b87431-9487-4ebe-9410-b3d9ebd63684: ``` 1. Parent /v1/runs dispatched two background subagents (deleg_0f180483, deleg_4683083e). 2. Parent turn ended normally: assistant asked for confirmation / Stage 1, finish_reason=stop, SSE event.complete. 3. Executor finished first. Wake self-POST arrived while the parent was still generating; the session lock queued it until complete. 4. Same second: a user row was inserted: [ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE — deleg_4683083e], including You may have moved on since dispatching — act. 5. Compression marked the confirmation assistant message compacted. Next assistant: skipped Confirm UI and called write_file. ``` No human message between complete and the skip-ahead turn. ### Affected Component Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) _No response_ ### Debug Report ```shell (base) user@host hermes-agent % hermes -p 4d5d09bd-ab39-480a-9d90-5d3db76bc20f debug share --lines 2000 --local Collecting debug report... The lock queued the wake until parent complete; it did not create the user-turn re-entry. Gateway log (timing): 10:41:45 Executor child finished 10:41:46 wake self-POST started; parent still in API call (confirmation text) 10:42:23 parent turn complete (response_len=1292, SSE /events closed) 10:42:23 same second: wake runs, history=28, user=[ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE — deleg_4683083e] 10:42:34 compression + message-alternation repair 10:43:06 assistant continues: skip Confirm UI, write_file SessionDB order: parent confirm assistant → wake user (BATCH COMPLETE + act) → confirm text compacted → assistant skips confirm. I can attach redacted gateway.log / session export if useful. Please ignore secrets in any debug-share paste. ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) api_server cannot push, so deliver_wake self-POSTs the completion through the same entry point as a real user turn: wake.py Lines 97-134 ``` async def _self_post_chat_completion( adapter: Any, *, text: str, session_id: str ) -> None: ... url = f"http://{host}:{port}/v1/chat/completions" ... payload = { "model": str(getattr(adapter, "_model_name", "") or "hermes-agent"), "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": text}], "stream": False, } ``` The formatted text is an imperative user message (tools/process_registry.py): ``` [ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE — {deleg_id}] ... You may have moved on since dispatching — act on these or re-dispatch ... ``` Call chain: completion_queue drain → deliver_wake (non-push) → _self_post_chat_completion → _run_agent. After the parent is idle, nothing distinguishes this from a human /v1/chat/completions. Skill “wait for confirm” is prompt-only. A new role=user turn is a continue signal. Related, not sufficient: [#84876](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/84876) / [#84235](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/84235) — serialize / stale snapshot. Reloading history after the lock still sees BATCH COMPLETE + act. [#77800](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/77800) — wake idempotency. A successful wake is still a user turn. [#40946](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/40946) / [#52756](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/52756) — idle auto-resume is intentional on push surfaces. Question: should api_server share that contract after event.complete? [#63671](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/63671) — TUI turn-origin / defer; only max_iterations_reached, not “waiting for confirm”, and not api_server. ### Proposed Fix (optional) Independent follow-up. Do not fold into [#84876](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/84876). Wanted, scoped to the non-push / api_server self-POST path: 1. Persist the completion on the session (reuse the durable completion ledger). Do not start a model turn. 2. On the next client /v1/runs or /v1/chat/completions, prepend pending completion(s) as context (not as the user’s confirmation). 3. Soften the template so it is not permission to pass a pending human gate. Prompt-only; not the gate. 4. Leave Telegram/Discord idle auto-resume unchanged. Leave the lock PR as serialize-only. Not proposing: banning async subagents in “blocking” skills (breaks background-load + foreground-confirm); a core Confirm primitive in this fix. Maintainer question: is api_server after event.complete “client owns the next turn,” or should it keep #40946 auto-resume? If the former, I can send a PR for (1)+(2). ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: [Bug]: Windows cron script execution uses base Python with PYTHONPATH, ignoring .pth files from editable installs
signals.text: ### Bug Description `cron/scheduler.py::_run_job_script` runs script jobs using `sys.executable`. On Windows environments where a virtual environment was created with `uv`, `_windows_cron_python_invocation` (around line 2162 of `cron/scheduler.py`) bypasses the venv launcher, invokes the base Python interpreter directly, and attempts to re-attach the venv by setting `PYTHONPATH` to its `site-packages`. However, `PYTHONPATH` entries are standard directory additions on `sys.path`. Python's site initialization does NOT process `.pth` files for paths added solely via `PYTHONPATH` — that only occurs for genuine site directories via `site.addsitedir()`. As a result, every editable package installed in the virtualenv (`pip install -e ...` / `.pth` links) is invisible to cron script jobs, resulting in `ModuleNotFoundError`. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a `uv` virtualenv on Windows. 2. Install a package in editable mode (`pip install -e <path>`). 3. Configure a cron script job (`no_agent: true` or python script) that imports the editable package. 4. Execute the cron job via the scheduler. ### Actual Behavior Under the base interpreter + scheduler's `PYTHONPATH`: - Standard non-editable packages (e.g. `yaml`): OK - Root on `PYTHONPATH` (`hermes_cli`): OK - Editable packages: `ModuleNotFoundError` ### Expected Behavior Editable packages installed in the virtual environment should be importable by scheduled cron scripts. ### Root Cause Analysis In `cron/scheduler.py`: `_windows_cron_python_invocation` sets `PYTHONPATH` but does not invoke `site.addsitedir()` on the venv site-packages. ### Proposed Fix In the script execution runner or Python invocation wrapper, ensure `site.addsitedir()` is called for the virtualenv's `site-packages` directory before script execution, ensuring `.pth` files are processed. ### Affected Component - Gateway / Cron / Tools - Operating System: Windows

signals.title: [Bug]: approvals.deny rules can be bypassed via repeated whitespace or tab characters
signals.text: ### Bug Description `tools/approval.py::_match_user_deny_rule` matches `approvals.deny` glob patterns against command strings using `fnmatch.fnmatchcase`. The command deobfuscation pipeline collapses quote-splitting, backslash escapes, ANSI sequences, and Unicode tricks, but it does **not** collapse repeated whitespace or tab characters. Because `fnmatch` cannot represent "one or more whitespace characters", any deny glob written with literal spaces between arguments (e.g. `git push --force origin main` or `gh repo delete <repo>`) can be completely bypassed by inserting an additional space or a tab. Since `approvals.deny` is designed as the tier-1 un-bypassable floor (evaluated ahead of `--yolo`, `/yolo`, and `approvals.mode=off`), this allows dangerous or irreversible commands to execute without approval if separated by whitespace variations. ### Steps to Reproduce / Measured Variants Evaluate against a standard 6-glob deny list with single spaces: - `git push --force origin main` -> BLOCKED (canonical control) - `git push --force origin main` (double space) -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `git\tpush --force origin main` (tab) -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `git push -f origin main` -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `git push --force origin main` -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `git\tpush\t-f origin main` -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `gh repo delete someorg/somerepo` -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `GIT PUSH --FORCE origin main` -> **NOT BLOCKED** - ` git push --force origin main` (leading whitespace) -> **NOT BLOCKED** 8 of 11 tested whitespace variants bypassed the single-space deny globs. `detect_hardline_command` also returned `False` for all of these variants. ### Expected Behavior Commands matching deny patterns should be blocked regardless of whether arguments are separated by single spaces, multiple spaces, or tabs. ### Root Cause Analysis `_match_user_deny_rule` in `tools/approval.py` runs `fnmatch` directly on the deobfuscated string without whitespace normalization. ### Proposed Fix Collapse contiguous whitespace characters before running `fnmatch`, e.g.: ```python candidate_normalized = " ".join(candidate.split()) ``` (This pattern is already used in `terminal_tool.py:2097`). Additionally, document that deny globs are evaluated against whitespace-collapsed strings so rules do not intentionally include multi-space strings. ### Affected Component - Tools / Approvals / Security
signals.author: WzKyy

signals.title: [Bug]: Gateway detachment diagnostics on Windows: stdin_is_tty is misleading and breakaway fallback is silent
signals.text: ### Bug Description While investigating gateway supervisor lifecycles on Windows, two detachment diagnostics and lifecycle issues were identified: 1. **`stdin_is_tty` in `gateway-exit-diag.log` is a misleading detachment diagnostic on Windows.** `gateway.py:4942` records `_stdin_is_tty = bool(sys.stdin and sys.stdin.isatty())` into every `gateway.start` record. On Windows, `os.isatty()` returns `True` for any character device, and `NUL` / `subprocess.DEVNULL` is a character device. A properly detached child process spawned with `windows_detach_flags()` (`0x09000200`) and `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` reports `stdin_is_tty: True` even though it has no attached console (`GetConsoleWindow() == 0`). The field only differentiates `pythonw.exe` (`sys.stdin is None` -> `False`) from `python.exe` (`True`), giving a misleading impression that a detached background gateway process remains attached to a terminal. 2. **Silent breakaway fallback in `_spawn_detached` leaves the gateway attached to launcher Job Objects.** In `gateway_windows.py:952-969`, if spawning with `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` fails with `OSError`, the spawn is retried with `windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()`. While falling back is reasonable, nothing is logged and no indicator is recorded in `gateway.start`. When launched from environments that use Windows Job Objects (e.g. Electron desktop app, Tauri installer, certain terminal emulators), the gateway silently remains in the parent job object. When the parent job owner exits, the gateway is terminated immediately by Windows with no exit record written to `gateway-exit-diag.log`. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. **For `stdin_is_tty`:** Spawn a child with `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | DETACHED_PROCESS` and `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL`. Inspect `sys.stdin.isatty()` — it returns `True`. 2. **For Breakaway Fallback:** Launch the gateway inside a nested job object that forbids breakaway. Observe that fallback occurs with 0 log messages and no metadata indicating breakaway failed. ### Expected Behavior - Diagnostics should accurately report whether a console/TTY is attached on Windows (e.g. via `GetConsoleWindow` or checking `HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED`). - Breakaway fallback should log a `WARNING` and record whether `breakaway` succeeded in the `gateway.start` record. ### Proposed Fix - In `gateway.py`: Replace raw `isatty()` on Windows with a check using `ctypes.windll.kernel32.GetConsoleWindow()` or `msvcrt`, and record `HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED`. - In `gateway_windows.py`: Log a warning when falling back to `windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()`, and add a `breakaway: true/false` field to the startup diagnostic payload. ### Affected Component - Gateway / CLI - Platform: Windows
signals.author: WzKyy

signals.title: [Bug]: Local model server connection errors fall through to unhelpful generic chat reply
signals.text: ### Bug Description `_gateway_provider_error_reply` (`gateway/run.py:522-536`) maps upstream model provider failures to concise, user-friendly chat responses across gateway channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, etc.). It currently contains dedicated branches for: - Authentication failures - Provider policy rejections - Rate limiting (429) All other errors fall through to the generic catch-all at line 536: > *"The model provider failed after retries. I kept raw provider details out of chat, check gateway logs for diagnostics."* For local/self-hosted model deployments (e.g. `llama.cpp`, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio running locally on `http://127.0.0.1:8033/v1`), the most common failure mode is that the local model server is simply not running or crashed. In this scenario, direct network connection errors (`httpx.ConnectError`, `openai.APIConnectionError`, `WinError 10061: target machine actively refused it`) are caught and properly classified in the core conversation loop, but are collapsed into the generic catch-all at the gateway reply layer. Directing a user on a mobile chat channel (away from the machine) to "check gateway logs for diagnostics" provides no actionable feedback when the server is just offline. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure Hermes with a local model endpoint (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8033/v1`). 2. Stop the local model server process. 3. Send a message to the agent via a gateway channel or a2a. ### Actual Behavior After retries, the user receives: > *"The model provider failed after retries. I kept raw provider details out of chat, check gateway logs for diagnostics."* Underlying error in conversation loop: `APIConnectionError` / `ConnectError` (WinError 10061). ### Expected Behavior The chat reply should clearly notify the user that the model endpoint is unreachable / not running. ### Proposed Fix Add a dedicated branch in `_gateway_provider_error_reply` before the catch-all for connection errors (`openai.APIConnectionError`, `httpx.ConnectError`, etc.): ```python if is_connection_error: return f"The model server at {configured_base_url} is not responding — it looks like it is not running." ``` ### Affected Component - Gateway - Agent Core / Configuration

signals.title: [Bug][Windows] TUI mouse wheel and selection fail under Windows Terminal/ConPTY
signals.text: ## Environment - OS: Windows 11 - Terminal: Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0 - Hermes Agent: v0.19.0 - Runtime path: native Windows / ConPTY - Config: `display.mouse_tracking: buttons` - No `HERMES_TUI_MOUSE_TRACKING`, `HERMES_TUI_DISABLE_MOUSE`, or `HERMES_TUI_INLINE` override initially ## Bug When running `hermes --tui` in Windows Terminal: - `PgUp/PgDn` scroll the transcript normally. - The mouse wheel does not scroll at all. - Mouse dragging cannot create a selectable/copyable text selection. - Enabling Windows Terminal `copyOnSelect` does not help because no selection is created. ## Reproduction 1. Open a native Windows Terminal tab. 2. Run `hermes --tui` with `display.mouse_tracking: buttons`. 3. Produce enough output to make the transcript scrollable. 4. Try the mouse wheel and drag over transcript text. ## Evidence A raw Node stdin probe enabled DECSET `1000`, `1002`, `1003`, and `1006` and ran for 90 seconds. Normal keyboard input (`a`, `b`, `c`, Enter) arrived, but zero mouse sequences arrived while testing wheel and drag input. This indicates that the failure occurs in the Windows Terminal/ConPTY mouse-event delivery path rather than in Hermes transcript scrolling itself. ## Workaround The following workaround restores native terminal scrollback, mouse selection, and copying on the same machine: ```powershell [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('HERMES_TUI_INLINE', '1', 'User') ``` After fully restarting Windows Terminal and launching `hermes --tui`, mouse scrolling and selection work. ## Expected behavior The TUI should either receive mouse events reliably under Windows Terminal/ConPTY, or provide a documented/fallback mode that preserves mouse wheel scrolling and native text selection/copying. Related: #4064, #83651

signals.title: [Bug]: Desktop retry of a failed turn silently truncates history via ordinal-only path — row-id guard (#83785) does not cover it
signals.text: ## Bug Description With #83785 merged, deliberate edits/rewinds are protected by durable `truncate_before_row_id` addressing + 4018/4030 refusals. But the **retry / plain-resubmit path after a failed turn** still travels the ordinal-only back-compat path, and a stale ordinal mis-aimed a real truncation in production: a retry of a 429-failed turn silently discarded 68 messages (4 user-turns deeper than intended) from the model's context. This is the residual hole of #82959 (auto-closed by the #83785 merge): the client and server ordinal address spaces had diverged, and because no row id was attached on this path, neither cross-check could fire. ## Incident (2026-08-14, Windows Desktop, kimi-k3 long session with prior in-place compactions) 1. `23:49:36` — user submits a normal new message; agent turn starts. 2. `23:50:21–23:50:47` — turn dies on HTTP 429 after 3 retries (`API call failed after 3 retries ... msgs=602`). 3. `23:53:37` — user re-attempts the failed turn. Gateway log: `prompt.submit: truncating session … history 600 -> 532 messages (ordinal=19)`. 4. **No new user text was persisted with that submit** (verified in `state.db`: the only rows stamped `23:53:37` are rebuild copies of earlier messages). 5. The cut deactivated 68 rows starting from a user message sent at **22:56** — four user-turns *before* the message being retried — silently dropping 3 subsequent user messages plus ~48 min of agent work from the model's active context. 6. The Desktop transcript still shows all discarded messages in original order (renderer state), so from the user's side the history looked intact; the model later discovered side effects (files, wiki edits, background processes) it had no memory of — a confusing divergence. Data was fully recoverable thanks to `archive_dropped` from #82950 — that safeguard worked exactly as intended. ## Expected Behavior Any submit that truncates should be addressed durably (row id) regardless of which client path initiates it (edit / regenerate / retry-after-error / plain resubmit with leaked composer state). If a row id can't be supplied, the gateway should refuse rather than trust an ordinal whose address space may have drifted from the renderer's. ## Analysis - The ordinal the client sent (`19`) was presumably correct in the renderer's *visible* user-message list, but the gateway counts all `role==user` non-`display_kind` rows — after in-place compactions, rebuild copies, and branch hiding, the two lists no longer align, so ordinal 19 resolved to different messages on each side. Exactly the drift #82959 catalogued. - `planEdit` (use-prompt-actions) attaches `source.rowId` for edits, and the failed-turn case (`isFailedTurn`) deliberately sends **no** truncation — but the observed submit did truncate with an ordinal and no row id, so it came from a path where the truncate state wasn't cleared and no durable id was attached (retry/resubmit with leaked composer rewind state, matching the #82756 mechanism). - Suggestions: (a) thread `rowId` through retry/resubmit/regenerate paths too; (b) clear composer truncate state when a turn fails; (c) gateway-side strict mode: refuse ordinal-only truncation (`4004`) for sessions whose history carries row ids.
