signals.title: Kanban project worktrees start from stale local HEAD instead of fetched origin/main
signals.text: ## Bug New project-linked Kanban task worktrees are created from the primary checkout's incidental `HEAD`, even when local `main` is stale/diverged from protected `origin/main`. ## Exact evidence - `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::_ensure_git_worktree` uses: `git -C <repo> worktree add -b <task-branch> <target> HEAD` - Project repo local `main`: `acd76b8dcdf23e963bc7105e042d414850331c99` - Protected `origin/main`: `8bf26916260358e731910bcf1b6d93d72b604a58` - Newly created project tasks `t_b725d07a` and `t_37018d67` both started at the stale local SHA. Their clean worktrees required incident recovery to the protected remote tip. ## Expected invariant For a new project-linked task branch, fetch `origin` first and base the branch on fetched `origin/main` (or the fetched symbolic remote default for non-main repositories). Existing task branches must be reused unchanged so retries remain idempotent and in-flight work is never discarded. Local-only repositories may retain `HEAD` fallback. ## Reproduction A regression test creates a repository with a bare `origin`, advances remote `main`, independently advances local `main`, calls `_ensure_git_worktree`, and compares the new worktree HEAD to `origin/main`. Current upstream behavior fails because the new branch equals local `main`. ## Validated patch A local patch introduces `_worktree_base_ref`, fetches/prunes `origin`, prefers verified `refs/remotes/origin/main^{commit}`, falls back to the fetched symbolic remote default, and uses that ref only for new branches. Targeted result: 10 tests passed across worktree isolation, project linking, and board-project scoping; Ruff and `git diff --check` pass. Local patch commit: `149221ff8b8fd233b8824cde3fc73b30a3250294` (not published).
signals.author: sammyhass

signals.title: Strip encrypted reasoning tokens from conversation context on cross-provider delegation and model switch
signals.text: ## Problem When the model is switched mid-session (e.g. from Anthropic to GPT to GLM via OpenRouter), the conversation history contains encrypted reasoning tokens from the previous provider. These tokens are opaque blobs that only the original provider's API can decrypt. When delegation passes this context to a subagent on a different provider, the new provider rejects the request: ``` HTTP 404: Your request contains encrypted reasoning or compaction content that was produced under a different model. Encrypted payloads can only be replayed to the endpoint that created them. ``` This kills all downstream delegation after a model switch. The subagent never runs — it fails before its first API call. ## Root cause `drop_thinking_only_and_merge_users` (in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:1355`) strips assistant turns that contain ONLY thinking/reasoning blocks with no visible content. But it does NOT strip encrypted reasoning blocks from turns that also contain real text or tool calls. Those turns pass through with the encrypted reasoning still attached, and the new provider rejects them. ## Why the encrypted reasoning is not needed Encrypted reasoning tokens are provider-internal state (Anthropic extended thinking, OpenAI o-series encrypted reasoning). They are opaque to any other provider and to the agent itself. The subagent needs only: - Plain-text user messages - Plain-text assistant responses (content + tool calls) - Tool call results - The task description (goal + context) All of these are fully portable across providers. The encrypted reasoning adds zero value to cross-provider calls and actively breaks them. ## Proposed fix When the provider changes mid-session, or when delegating to a subagent on a different provider, strip all encrypted reasoning/thinking blocks from assistant turns in the conversation context before sending. Keep the plain-text content, tool calls, and tool results intact. Specifically, in the API message preparation path (before the cross-provider call), for each assistant message that has thinking/reasoning blocks: 1. Remove all blocks of type `thinking`, `redacted_thinking`, `reasoning_content`, `reasoning_details`, `codex_reasoning_items` from the content 2. Keep all `text`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, and other non-reasoning blocks 3. If the turn ends up with no content after stripping (thinking-only), it gets dropped by the existing `drop_thinking_only_and_merge_users` logic This makes model switching mid-session safe for delegation, context compression, background review, and any other feature that replays conversation history to a different provider. ## Reproduction 1. Start a session on Anthropic Claude (with extended thinking enabled) 2. Switch the model to GPT-5.6 or GLM-5.2 via OpenRouter mid-session 3. Call `delegate_task` — the subagent fails with HTTP 404 encrypted reasoning error ## Environment - Hermes agent with OpenRouter as the provider - Model switching mid-session (Anthropic → GPT/GLM) - Delegation to subagents on a different provider than the original
signals.author: mikejflex

signals.title: [Bug]: Desktop — "↓ needs approval" floating bar reappears after the turn finished (stale per-session approval entry)
signals.text: ## Bug Description After a session's turn has finished (sidebar shows the green "finished — unread" dot), the in-chat **"↓ needs approval" floating bar** (the floating approval fallback with "Run / Deny" buttons, pinned above the composer) keeps appearing. Scrolling the transcript makes it appear and disappear repeatedly: - Scroll to the area with the tool row that raised the approval → the inline approval bar mounts → the floating bar hides. - Scroll away (e.g. to the bottom where the final "finished" message is) → the floating bar reappears. So a finished session can still show a phantom "needs approval" prompt that the user can't act on meaningfully (the turn is over). ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Hermes Desktop v0.20.1 (2eda129), Windows 10, local gateway. 2. Run a session whose turn triggers an approval-gated terminal command. Do not respond to the approval (or let the command resolve through the smart-approval path without a manual `approval.respond`). 3. Let the turn finish normally (the agent times out the approval and completes, or the approval is resolved without a respond round-trip). 4. Scroll the transcript: leaving the tool-row area shows the "↓ needs approval" floating bar again; scrolling back to the tool row hides it. The sidebar already shows the session as finished (green dot). ## Expected Behavior Once the turn ends (or the approval is resolved), all approval UI for that session — including the floating fallback bar — should disappear permanently. A finished session must never show a "needs approval" prompt. ## Actual Behavior The floating approval bar keeps appearing based on scroll position, driven by a stale per-session approval entry that was never cleared. ## Additional Context Source facts (Desktop, v0.20.1): - The floating bar is `PendingApprovalFallback` (`apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/approval.tsx`): it renders whenever `sessionApprovalRequest(sessionId)` is non-null AND no inline anchor is mounted (`!request || inlineVisible → null`). - The inline bar (`PendingToolApproval`) only mounts when the pending tool row is actually rendered in the virtualized transcript (it calls `registerApprovalInlineAnchor` in an effect). Scrolling the tool row out of view unmounts it, so the floating fallback reappears — this is the scroll-dependent flicker. - Clear paths for the per-session approval entry: `message.complete` / `error` → `clearAllPrompts(sessionId)` (`gateway-event.ts`), and `approval.respond` → `clearApprovalRequest(request.sessionId)`. - Suspected causes for the stale entry (unverified which one fires in practice): - An approval resolved via the smart-approval path or by timeout is never followed by an `approval.respond` round-trip, so `clearApprovalRequest` never runs; whether `message.complete` clears it depends on the session key matching (below). - `session.resume` mints a fresh random runtime id every time (`tui_gateway/methods_session.py`: `sid = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]` on the cold/lazy/eager resume paths). The approval entry is stored under the runtime session id that raised it. If the same stored session is resumed again (tab reopen, tile ↔ main switch, app restart) the runtime id rotates, and the `message.complete` clear for the new runtime id cannot remove an entry keyed by the old one. Related: #86565 — the same approval state machine family: the sidebar dot never turns amber while an approval is pending (its root cause is the `session.active_list` status mapping; this issue is the stale-entry / clear-path family).
signals.author: linfeng961

signals.title: Windows: kanban dispatcher-spawned worker crashes ~60s after spawn (pid not alive) even for trivial tasks; same profile works when launched manually
signals.text: ### Summary On **Windows**, kanban dispatcher-spawned worker agents crash ~40-60s after spawn with `pid <n> not alive`, even for trivial tasks. The worker process genuinely exits (PID no longer exists in the system), and the task goes `blocked` after `max_retries` consecutive failures. The **same profile works perfectly when launched manually** (`hermes -p <profile> chat -q "..."` runs to completion), so the profile, credentials, and model provider are not the cause — the failure is specific to the dispatcher-spawned subprocess path on Windows. ### Environment - OS: Windows (RDP session), Hermes git-installed at `~/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent` - Python: Hermes venv 3.11 - Model provider: custom `fennoai-copy` (OpenAI-compatible) — verified working (HTTP 200) with the profile's key - Kanban: board `codex-alpha-factory`, worker profiles `factory-*` created via `hermes profile create <name> --clone` - Hermes version: (current git checkout) ### Repro (minimal) 1. `hermes profile create factory-db --clone` (worker profile) 2. `hermes -p factory-db gateway run` (worker profile gateway running; dispatcher is embedded in it) 3. Create a trivial task: `hermes kanban create "worker-smoke-test-echo" --assignee factory-db` 4. `hermes kanban dispatch --max 1` 5. Wait ~60s → run outcome `crashed`, error `pid <n> not alive`, task auto-blocks after 2 failures. Observed with a task whose entire body was "echo a line and complete" — no DB, no long-running work. ### What we observed - Worker log (`kanban/boards/<board>/logs/<task>.log`) shows the agent **starts normally**: reads the task card (`kanban_show`), loads skills, begins working — then the process disappears. - `task_runs` rows: every crashed run has `elapsed ≈ 37s, 61s, 122s, 182s` — a fixed ~60s cadence, matching the dispatcher's 60s tick. The dispatcher checks `_pid_alive(worker_pid)` (Windows path: `OpenProcess` via `gateway.status._pid_exists`) and finds the PID gone. - `tasks.worker_pid` becomes NULL and `last_heartbeat_at` stops updating shortly after start — the worker either never established heartbeat or exited within ~1 minute. - The worker profile's gateway IS running (`hermes profile list` shows `running`); the dispatcher log shows `spawned=1` then `crashed=1`. - **Control experiment:** `timeout 95 hermes -p factory-db chat -q "sleep 5 ..."` runs to completion (42s, exit 0) with the same profile, same model, same credentials. Manual launch = stable; dispatcher spawn = dies in ~1 min. ### Suspected cause (needs maintainer input) The dispatcher spawns the worker as a subprocess of the long-lived gateway. On Windows something in that path either: 1. kills the child when the parent/console session interacts (e.g. `TERMINAL_CWD` deprecation warning path, console-group signal handling — note the code explicitly avoids `os.kill(pid, 0)` on Windows for this reason, bpo-14484), or 2. the worker never registers a heartbeat (`heartbeat_claim`) in time, so the 60s liveness sweep marks it crashed even though it may still be initializing (model handshake / skill loading can exceed 60s on cold start), or 3. the worker subprocess inherits a broken environment from the gateway (e.g. `TERMINAL_CWD` pointing at the scratch workspace, or missing env that the interactive shell provides). The fixed 60s cadence across all crashes (regardless of task size) makes a heartbeat-timing issue very plausible: the worker's first heartbeat must arrive within the dispatcher tick, and on Windows cold-start model/auth init may exceed it. ### Suggested investigation 1. Log the worker subprocess's actual exit code / stderr when `_pid_alive` fails (currently only `pid N not alive` is recorded, losing the real exit reason). 2. Confirm whether the worker calls `heartbeat_claim` before doing anything else, and whether the dispatcher grants a grace period > 1 tick before declaring a crash. 3. Check whether spawning with a fresh `TERMINAL_CWD` / clean env (the deprecation warning suggests `.env` leaks into the worker) changes survival. 4. Consider a `--no-gateway` / detached worker mode on Windows, or a longer initial liveness grace. ### Impact - Any kanban board whose worker profiles are on Windows cannot rely on auto-dispatch: every task goes `blocked` after 2 crashes, requiring manual intervention (the user must go tell the work-station session, then the same work is done manually). - Blocks multi-agent workflows (orchestrator → kanban → worker profiles) on Windows entirely.
signals.author: Victor-lys

signals.title: Gateway auto-resume persists an empty user message that triggers Pre-call sanitizer on every subsequent turn
signals.text: ## Summary When the gateway restarts with a `resume_pending` session (e.g. the daily 05:58 SIGKILL/OOM restart on Termux), `_schedule_resume_pending_sessions` synthesizes an inbound message with empty text. The gateway's resume branch in `gateway/run.py` correctly replaces `ctx.message` with a `build_resume_recovery_note()` system note for the **model**, but it persists the **original empty user message** to `state.db` via `_persist_user_message_override = ctx.message` (line 5818, set before the replacement). Once that empty user row is in the transcript, the Pre-call sanitizer (`repair_empty_non_final_messages` in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`) heals it **in memory** on every subsequent API call — but the stored history is never mutated (by design). So the same empty message triggers the warning on **every turn** for the rest of the session's life. ## Impact - 26 `Pre-call sanitizer: healed 1 empty non-final message(s)` warnings + 3 `Persisted transcript lagged live cached history` warnings in one QQ DM session over a ~2-hour window. - The sanitizer prevents actual 400 errors (its job), so there is **no functional breakage** — but the session is permanently noisy in logs. - The disk-vs-memory count offset (`disk=129, memory=130`) is also permanent for that session. ## Root cause `gateway/run.py` line 5816–5833: ```python if _is_resume_pending: _reason = getattr(_resume_entry, "resume_reason", None) or "restart_timeout" _persist_user_message_override = ctx.message # ← line 5818: captures ORIGINAL empty text # ... adapter-awareness ... ctx.message = build_resume_recovery_note( # ← replaces what the MODEL sees _reason, ctx.message, interactive=_interactive_resume, ) ``` Then at line 5925–5926: ```python if _persist_user_message_override is not None: _conversation_kwargs["persist_user_message"] = _persist_user_message_override ``` So the **recovery note goes to the model**, but the **empty string goes to the database**. The override is captured before the replacement. ## Evidence ### 1. Gateway log — empty message synthesized at restart ``` 2026-08-14 05:58:49,503 INFO gateway.run: Scheduled auto-resume for 1 restart-interrupted session(s) 2026-08-14 05:58:49,855 INFO gateway.run: inbound message: platform=qqbot user=B74A939C8E1A66816031EE86D6F1C6F4 chat=B74A939C8E1A66816031EE86D6F1C6F4 msg='' reply_to_id=None reply_to_text='' ``` ### 2. Database — empty user message persisted ``` sqlite3 state.db "SELECT id, role, length(content) AS clen FROM messages WHERE session_id='20260724_094354_caf1ed0c' AND role='user' AND (content='' OR content IS NULL);" id role clen 106935 user 0 ``` Timestamp: `2026-08-14 05:59:14` — exactly at the auto-resume window. ### 3. Sanitizer warnings — same session, 26 times over 2 hours ``` 2026-08-14 19:14:30,606 WARNING [20260724_094354_caf1ed0c] run_agent: Pre-call sanitizer: healed 1 empty non-final message(s) by substituting placeholder content — ... 2026-08-14 20:46:18,586 WARNING [20260724_094354_caf1ed0c] run_agent: Pre-call sanitizer: healed 1 empty non-final message(s) ... ``` ### 4. Disk-vs-memory lag — same session, offset is always +1 ``` 2026-08-14 19:14:30,522 WARNING [20260724_094354_caf1ed0c] gateway.run: Persisted transcript lagged live cached history for session agent:main:qqbot:dm:B74A939C8E1A66816031EE86D6F1C6F4 (disk=129, memory=130) 2026-08-14 20:36:37,934 WARNING [...] (disk=131, memory=132) 2026-08-14 20:38:17,124 WARNING [...] (disk=139, memory=140) ``` ## Affected sessions Five QQ DM sessions with the same empty-user-message pattern: | Session | Source | Timestamp of empty user msg | |---|---|---| | `20260716_184517_caedbb` | qqbot | 2026-07-16 18:53:10 | | `20260716_192100_97db90` | qqbot | 2026-07-16 18:53:10 | | `20260716_192331_993eb8` | qqbot | 2026-07-16 18:53:10 | | `20260716_194449_d51a00` | qqbot | 2026-07-16 18:53:10 | | `20260724_094354_caf1ed0c` | qqbot | 2026-08-14 05:59:14 | ## Related issues - #82924 — Pre-call sanitizer can emit an empty assistant message (tool_calls dedup → empty array). Different code path: that is about `sanitize_api_messages()` step 3 producing empty assistant `tool_calls`. This issue is about **persisting an empty USER message** from the gateway resume path. - #76862 — Same tool_calls-dedup root cause as #82924, not the same as this one. ## Suggested fix In the `_is_resume_pending` branch, persist the **recovery note** (or at minimum a non-empty placeholder) instead of the original empty `ctx.message`. For example, capture the override **after** the replacement: ```python if _is_resume_pending: _reason = getattr(_resume_entry, "resume_reason", None) or "restart_timeout" ctx.message = build_resume_recovery_note( _reason, ctx.message, interactive=_interactive_resume, ) _persist_user_message_override = ctx.message # ← persist the note, not the empty original ``` This ensures the database row is non-empty and the sanitizer never needs to fire. The same change should apply to the safety-net branch at line 5864–5875. ## Environment - Hermes Agent (latest main, Termux/Android) - Provider: omniroute (custom OpenAI-compatible) - Platform: qqbot (QQ DM) - Daily gateway restart at 05:58 CST (Termux SIGKILL/OOM)
signals.author: Jensenwgd

signals.title: [Bug]: Truncated-response continuation (finish_reason=length) never checks for repetition before retrying, and Discord delivery has no split-count cap — one degenerate turn floods a channel with 30+ messages
signals.text: ### Bug Description A single agent turn produced a final response of 60,698 characters, delivered to a live Discord channel as **31 separate messages** posted back-to-back. Reconstructed from `state.db` message rows and gateway logs, this happened in two independently-missing safety checks, not one: 1. **Generation side**: the model entered degenerate repetition mid-response, hit the provider's output-token ceiling (`finish_reason=length`), and Hermes's own truncation-continuation path retried it — appending a "continue, don't repeat" nudge — **without ever checking whether the content it was about to continue was already pathological**. 2. **Delivery side**: the resulting 60,757-char combined response was hard to miss (Discord's own 2000-char limit forces a split), yet the platform adapter splits and sends **every** resulting chunk with no upper bound on count. Either check alone would have prevented the user-facing flood. ### Root Cause (confirmed against `main` @ `76d832d3`, Hermes Agent v0.20.0 / 2026.8.3, cross-checked against `state.db` message rows for the affected session) **1. (Primary) `finish_reason=length` triggers an automatic continuation with zero content-sanity check on the truncated text.** Evidence from `state.db` (`messages` table, `session_id='20260814_142129_1a77534b'`): | id | role | len | finish_reason | timestamp (UTC) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 39020 | assistant | 57,752 | `length` | 14:56:05.907 | | 39021 | user (synthetic) | 176 | — | 14:56:05.907 (same instant) | | 39036 | assistant | 2,945 | `stop` | 14:58:24.877 | `57752 + 2945 = 60697` ≈ the `60698`-char final response the gateway delivered — the two fragments were stitched into one turn. Message 39020's content is not random garbage — it opens with `"We need to verify the model setting. The user wants ... Then '...' Then '...'"`: the model was narrating/summarizing the conversation so far, one prior user turn at a time. When it reached the point in history where the user had once said *"好，你幫我更改成 Google Gemini 4 31B。"* (said exactly **once**, at 14:33:33 — confirmed by scanning all 16 user-role rows in this session; there is no duplicate inbound message), it entered a token-level repetition loop echoing that fragment, verbatim, hundreds of times, consuming the rest of its output budget until the provider cut it off. Message 39021 is Hermes's own auto-injected continuation nudge — `agent/conversation_loop.py:781-785` (`_LENGTH_CONTINUATION_OUTPUT_LIMIT`): ```python _LENGTH_CONTINUATION_OUTPUT_LIMIT = ( "[System: Your previous response was truncated by the output " "length limit. Continue exactly where you left off. Do not " "restart or repeat prior text. Finish the answer directly.]" ) ``` This fires from the `finish_reason == "length"` branch at `agent/conversation_loop.py:3196`. The branch already contains a specific, targeted sanity check for a *different* pathological case — thinking-budget exhaustion (`_thinking_exhausted`, `conversation_loop.py:3196-3260`) — which aborts immediately with a user-facing `"⚠️ Thinking Budget Exhausted"` message instead of retrying. **No equivalent check exists for "the truncated content is dominated by repeated text."** The continuation path (`conversation_loop.py:3369-3412`, guarded only by `length_continue_retries < 4` at line 1576/3333) unconditionally appends the truncated fragment to `messages` and asks the model to keep going. In this incident it only needed 1 of the 4 available retries — the second pass finished cleanly (`finish_reason=stop`, no further repetition) — so the retry-count ceiling never engaged; nothing else was in a position to catch the first fragment's content quality before it was folded into the final response. **2. Delivery side: the chunk-send loop has no count/size ceiling either.** `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:1002-1003`: ```python MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 2000 _SPLIT_THRESHOLD = 1900 # near the 2000-char split point ``` `plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:3114-3122`: ```python # Format and split message if needed formatted = self.format_message(content) chunks = self.truncate_message(formatted, self.MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH) message_ids = [] reference = self._reply_reference_for_send(reply_to, channel) for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks): ``` `chunks` is iterated in full regardless of `len(chunks)`. No `if len(chunks) > N` guard exists here, in the structurally identical `_send_to_forum` path (line 3206), or the edit-overflow path (line 3473). A 2-chunk reply and a 200-chunk reply take the exact same code path. **3. The gateway's own split-delivery bookkeeping already *knows* a split is happening, but only uses that for a duplicate-suppression decision, not a circuit breaker.** `gateway/run.py:27059` (this incident's actual log line): ``` Stale streamed finalize detected for session %s on a multi-message split; skipping the in-place reconciliation edit and delivering the complete response via normal final send (#78541). ``` `_turn_split_delivery` (`gateway/run.py:27050-27059`) is a concrete, checked signal that the current response is being delivered as a multi-message split, available *before* the send happens. It is used only to pick edit-vs-fresh-send; never to ask "is this split unreasonably large?" **4. Response-shape validation exists but only checks structural validity, not content sanity.** `agent/conversation_loop.py:2786-2864` — `validate_response()` (dispatched per `api_mode`) checks for `response is None`, missing/empty `choices`, missing `content`, etc. A structurally well-formed response with `finish_reason=stop` and 60,698 chars of repeated text passes every check here. **5. Contributing factor — the turn ran to 108K tokens across 10 API calls with no early exit.** Before producing the oversized answer, the agent spent ~15 minutes retrying blocked tool calls (`hermes model` requiring a TTY; an internal guard rejecting self-restart from inside the gateway process). Nothing in the retry/iteration accounting (turn ended at `api_calls=10/90`, well under budget) treats "many consecutive tool failures without task progress" as a signal to stop and hand back a short, controlled error instead of continuing to grow context — the polluted, 100K+-token context is the substrate the repetition loop in #1 happened on top of. **6. Related, lower-confidence observation — not the cause of this incident, but same risk class.** `agent/background_review.py:3` documents that after most turns, `AIAgent.run_conversation` may fork a background self-review agent that replays the **full, unfiltered parent conversation snapshot** on the same model/runtime. `agent/background_review.py:757-758` shows the fork only inherits a `max_tokens` cap if the *parent* explicitly set one — no independent ceiling otherwise. In this incident the review fork for the same session was triggered 1.4s after the flood turn ended and was itself killed mid-call by a gateway restart (`Broken pipe` in the logs) before it produced anything — so it did not cause this flood, but it inherited the exact same 108K-token polluted snapshot and had no independent output-length guard either. Flagging as a related gap, not the root cause of this ticket. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Get a model into a state where, while narrating/summarizing prior conversation turns, it echoes one fragment repeatedly (long, error-laden context measurably increases the odds — see #5 above — but this is a model-degeneracy trigger, not a Hermes-specific one). 2. Let generation run to the provider's output-token ceiling (`finish_reason=length`) while still inside the repeated fragment. 3. Observe: `conversation_loop.py`'s length-continuation path retries automatically with no inspection of the truncated content (root cause #1). 4. Whether or not the continuation itself repeats, the stitched final response can already be tens of thousands of characters. Observe: the Discord adapter splits and sends **all** resulting chunks with no ceiling (root cause #2). Root cause #2 alone is trivially reproducible without reproducing model degeneracy: call `DiscordAdapter.send()` with any string >60,000 chars against a live channel and count outbound messages. ### Actual Behavior ``` state.db: id=39020 role=assistant len=57752 finish_reason=length (14:56:05.907 UTC) state.db: id=39021 role=user len=176 [System: ...truncated... Continue...] (same instant, synthetic) state.db: id=39036 role=assistant len=2945 finish_reason=stop (14:58:24.877 UTC) gateway.run: response ready: platform=discord chat=1537828505927033063 time=882.3s api_calls=10 response=60698 chars [Discord] Sending response (60757 chars) to 1537828505927033063 → 31 individual Discord messages posted back-to-back ``` ### Expected Behavior 1. In the `finish_reason == "length"` branch (`conversation_loop.py:3196`), before appending the continuation nudge, run a cheap content-sanity check on the truncated fragment (e.g. n-gram repetition ratio, or simply: longest exact substring repeated >K times) analogous to the existing `_thinking_exhausted` check at the same call site. On a pathological result, abort the turn with a short, user-facing error (same pattern as the existing `"⚠️ Thinking Budget Exhausted"` message) instead of continuing. 2. Independently, `DiscordAdapter.send()` (and the identical `_send_to_forum` / edit-overflow paths) should cap the number of chunks sent for one logical response — e.g. a configurable `max_split_messages` (suggested default: 5-8) — falling back to a short "response was abnormally large, see logs" notice instead of flooding. 3. The existing `_turn_split_delivery` bookkeeping in `gateway/run.py` already has the chunk context needed to enforce (2) platform-agnostically at the gateway layer instead of duplicating it per-adapter. ### Proposed Fix (sketch, for a follow-up PR) 1. Add a bounded repetition check (e.g. `agent/repetition_guard.py`, called from `conversation_loop.py:3196` right after `_thinking_exhausted` is ruled out) gating the length-continuation path. 2. Add `DiscordAdapter.MAX_SPLIT_MESSAGES` (or a shared constant in `gateway/platforms/base.py`) checked right after `chunks = self.truncate_message(...)` at `adapter.py:3116`, `3206`, `3473`. 3. Optionally surface `_turn_split_delivery`'s chunk count in `gateway/run.py` before calling adapter `send()` so (2) can be enforced once, platform-agnostically. ### Environment - **Hermes Agent**: v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) · upstream commit `76d832d3857551a029c4b39c23945eb47c16fe5b` - **Install method**: Docker (`nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`) - **Platform**: Discord (guild channel, non-forum, non-thread — plain `channel.send()` path) - **Provider/model active during incident**: `nvidia` / `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning` (verified against a same-day NVIDIA `/v1/models` snapshot — model ID itself was valid; this is not a "model doesn't exist" report) - Verified via direct log + `state.db` inspection against the exact running commit (matched `hermes version` output to `git log -1` in a full clone of upstream at that commit). ### Related Work - **#30408** — "Hermes should stop repeated tool loops and block obviously broken final responses." Closed 2026-06-28 as `completed`, **no linked PR**, maintainer (`teknium1`) declined the model-behavior framing verbatim: *"We don't want to fix models problems. There are also plenty of legitimate paths to repeat tool calls."* This report deliberately does not re-ask for model-output judgment. Root causes #1-#4 below are Hermes's own retry/validation/delivery code, independent of whether the model "should" have produced that output — the same distinction the maintainer's own closed **#10711** (below) already accepted for a structurally identical case. - **#10711** — "Ollama returns `finish_reason='stop'` on truncated GLM responses, causing agent to silently drop final output" (closed, `completed`). Established the precedent that Hermes must not blindly trust a provider's finish-signal and needs its own content-side verification before treating a response as final. Root cause #1 in this report asks for the same class of check on the *other* side of that precedent: `finish_reason=length` is correctly detected, but the continuation path still doesn't inspect the truncated content before retrying. - **#13208** (open, unresolved) + **#6784** / **#8528** (open PRs, unmerged: "tool loop detection with context pruning" / "integrate tool loop detection into agent loop") — cover contributing factor #5 (no-progress tool-call loops growing context unchecked). This report does not duplicate that ask; it references it only as background for why the turn reached 108K tokens before the repetition in #1 occurred. If #6784/#8528 land, they may reduce (but would not eliminate) exposure to #1 and #2 — the content-check and delivery-cap gaps are independent of whether the loop that grew the context gets shortened. - **#78541** — "Suppressing normal final send swallows complete replies on Telegram group/forum sessions" (closed, fixed via #79669) — established the `_turn_split_delivery` flag this incident's payload traveled through. That fix addressed a *suppression* bug (legitimate content silently dropped); this report is the opposite direction (oversized content delivered with no ceiling) through the same code path. - **#71643** — "Telegram streaming — successful finalize edit carries the stale preview text" (closed) — the stale-finalize reconciliation-edit fallback referenced in the same `gateway/run.py` block. - **#25349** — "Discord streaming can duplicate final responses across chunked delivery" (open) — same general code area, different symptom (duplication vs. unbounded volume). - **#75423** (open) — "`_SKILL_REVIEW_PROMPT` turns one-off investigations into documentation-shaped Skills" — a different symptom of the same background-review mechanism flagged as a related risk in root cause #6; corroborates that the review fork has more than one open edge case around what context/output it's trusted with. ### Additional Context - No pending/queued outbound messages were involved — this was a single turn's response, delivered once, not a retry loop re-sending old content. - The incident coincided with, but was not caused by, a global model configuration change and gateway restart the user performed shortly after (switching to `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b`, unrelated to the model active during the flood). Nothing in the user-facing output distinguished "this flood came from a turn already in flight" from "this flood came from the model you just switched to" — worth a documentation/UX note even outside this specific bug.
signals.author: vincentee91g

signals.title: [Bug]: Desktop auto-TTS reads the same reply again right after playback finishes
signals.text: ## Symptom With `voice.auto_tts: true` ("Read responses aloud"), a reply is read aloud a **second time from the beginning** right after its playback finishes. Every spoken reply is affected. ## Reproduction 1. Enable read-responses-aloud (`voice.auto_tts: true` in config.yaml). 2. Send any prompt in the desktop chat and let the reply be read aloud to the end. 3. When playback finishes, the same reply starts playing again. ## Root cause (source trace, main @ b6726d57e) Auto-speak dedupe is keyed on the renderer's message **row id**, which is volatile across the turn-end boundary: 1. `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-composer-voice.ts` — `lastSpokenIdRef` / `pendingResponse()` / `consumePendingResponse()` compare `last.id === lastSpokenIdRef.current`. 2. During streaming, the assistant row carries a live-tail id (`assistant-stream-*`; see `isLiveTailRow` in `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/utils.ts`, which explicitly contrasts it with "a committed transcript row"). When the text completes, `speakLatest` in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-auto-speak-replies.ts` marks **that** id spoken and starts playback. 3. At/after turn end, the authoritative flush reconciles the row via `reconcileResumeMessages()` — same bubble, same text, but the committed row's id replaces the `assistant-stream-*` id. 4. `use-auto-speak-replies.ts` also subscribes `$voicePlayback.listen(speakLatest)`. When playback ends, state transitions to `idle`, `speakLatest` fires, and `pendingResponse()` now sees the committed id ≠ `lastSpokenId` → the reply is treated as unspoken and played again. After the second playback the ids match, so it stops — which matches the observed "reads exactly twice" behavior. ### Sibling path with the same defect The manual **Read Aloud** button (`apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/assistant-message.tsx`, `ReadAloudButton`) calls `playSpeechText()` directly without marking the reply spoken. So manually reading the latest reply is likewise followed by an auto-speak replay on the playback-idle edge, whenever auto-speak hasn't already consumed that reply. ## Expected Each completed reply is spoken at most once, regardless of live→committed row-id reconciliation or manual reads. ## Fix direction Key spoken-state on something stable across the live→committed transition — e.g. the assistant role-ordinal of the turn, or a hash of the spoken text — or move spoken tracking into a shared per-session store that survives row identity changes; and have the manual read-aloud path mark the reply spoken too. Happy to discuss the exact key if a different invariant is preferred. ## Environment - Hermes Desktop 0.17.0, built from main @ b6726d57e (local build, 2026-08-15) - macOS (Apple Silicon) - TTS provider: MiniMax (also reproducible in principle with any provider — the defect is in the renderer's dedupe key, not synthesis)

signals.title: [Bug]: Desktop read-aloud speaks hardcoded English placeholders ("code block omitted", "link") and silently drops tables
signals.text: ## Symptom Desktop **Read Aloud** on a reply that contains a fenced code block speaks the English words **"code block omitted"** instead of the content; URLs are spoken as the English word **"link"**; and Markdown **tables are dropped entirely** with no spoken notice at all. For non-English users this is jarring: with a Chinese TTS voice, a lone English word ("omitted") is spoken where the user expects content, and table content silently vanishes from the audio. ## Root cause `apps/desktop/src/lib/speech-text.ts` hardcodes English placeholders and strips tables: - L4: `const CODE_BLOCK_SUMMARY = ' code block omitted '` - L156: fenced code blocks → `CODE_BLOCK_SUMMARY` - L160: `URL_RE` → `' link '` - `stripMarkdownTables()` (L102–143) removes entire tables from the speakable text with no placeholder The desktop app already ships an i18n system with multiple locales, but these strings bypass it. ## Expected - Placeholder phrases are localized through the desktop i18n system (or at minimum follow the UI locale). - Tables get a spoken notice (e.g. a localized "table omitted") instead of silent removal — or their header rows are read. ## Fix direction Route `CODE_BLOCK_SUMMARY` and the `' link '` replacement through the existing i18n layer, and emit a localized placeholder for stripped tables. Happy to discuss whether reading code/table content (possibly truncated) is preferable to a placeholder. ## Environment - Hermes Desktop 0.17.0, built from main @ b6726d57e (local build, 2026-08-15) - macOS (Apple Silicon), TTS provider: MiniMax, Chinese voice

signals.title: feat(desktop): local on-device STT (whisper) when connected to a remote backend
signals.text: ## Problem When Hermes Desktop is connected to a **remote backend** (e.g. a headless VPS via SSH/HTTP), voice dictation always sends the audio to the backend and transcribes there (`transcribeAudio()` in `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts` → `POST /api/audio/transcribe`). The desktop app itself has **no client-side transcription path**. Consequences: - Voice latency is bound by the network round-trip (Mac → VPS → STT → VPS → Mac), not by the transcription itself. - A local M-series Mac with whisper.cpp / faster-whisper / MLX (which would transcribe in ~1s) is forced to use the backend's STT stack instead. - On Apple Silicon this is a 5–10x worse experience than tools like Cursor/Claude Code, which transcribe on-device. - Users who want on-device STT must run the desktop in `local` mode (separate Hermes instance) — losing the shared memory/skills of their main backend. Related: - #80826 — Desktop voice transcription hardcodes OpenAI API (same root cause: desktop has no own STT path) - #70472 — adds command-provider setup UI, but providers still execute on the backend - #78207 (Vox Lockin, lane 09) — desktop voice reliability ## Proposal Add an optional **client-side STT path** in the desktop app: 1. New setting, e.g. `voice.dictation.stt: "backend" | "local"` (default `backend`, no behavior change). 2. In `local` mode, transcribe on-device using: - **whisper.cpp** binary (macOS/Windows), or - **faster-whisper** / **MLX whisper** on Apple Silicon. 3. Fallback chain: local engine → remote backend → error, so a missing model never bricks dictation. 4. Model/language options in Settings → Voice, reusing existing `stt.local.*` semantics. The desktop app already captures audio locally (mic → getUserMedia) and already ships a local backend child process — the missing piece is only *routing* the recorded audio to a local engine before falling back to the remote backend. ## Expected behavior User on a MacBook Pro connected to a remote VPS backend clicks the mic → audio is transcribed **on-device** in ~1s → text lands in the composer. The backend is untouched (agent, memory, skills still remote). Happy to implement and open a PR — I can have a working proof-of-concept (whisper.cpp/faster-whisper local path with backend fallback) ready.

signals.title: fix(lsp): repair native Windows npm launchers
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes native Windows LSP launcher discovery, stale-install repair, and batch execution. This is the focused launcher-only slice requested in the automated triage on August 3. - Prefer native npm launchers (`.exe`, `.com`, `.cmd`, `.bat`) over extensionless POSIX shims on Windows. - Keep npm wrappers in their canonical `node_modules/.bin` directory so `%~dp0`-relative package paths remain valid. - Treat a staged POSIX-only shim as stale and repair it from the canonical native wrapper. - Execute `.cmd` / `.bat` language servers, npm installers, and Node health probes through quoted child-only environment placeholders so spaces, `&`, and `%` are not reparsed as shell syntax. - Preserve native extensionless PE executables and existing non-Windows launcher behavior. Fixes #49470. ## Split from the previous combined PR The diagnostic transport and URI-identity changes formerly included here have moved to #81915. The two PRs are independent and can be reviewed or merged in either order. ## Root cause npm installs sibling launchers on Windows: an extensionless POSIX shell shim, a native `.cmd` wrapper, and often a `.ps1` wrapper. MSYS can report the extensionless shim as executable, but native Python passes it to Win32 `CreateProcess` and receives `WinError 193`. Hermes also copied npm wrappers into a staging directory. npm `.cmd` wrappers resolve their package entrypoint relative to `%~dp0`, so moving one can make a launchable process exit immediately because its package path no longer resolves. Finally, directly interpolating valid Windows paths into `cmd.exe` command lines allowed spaces and shell metacharacters to change argument boundaries. The shared helper passes each argument through the child environment and expands it inside quotes instead. ## Verification Tested on native Windows against current `upstream/main`: ```text Focused launcher regression suite: 24 passed Complete LSP suite: 77 passed, 1 deselected Combined launcher + diagnostics suite: 94 passed, 1 skipped, 1 deselected Targeted constants regression: 1 passed Ruff: all checks passed Git diff check: clean ``` GitHub CI [run 31272691192](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/31272691192) is currently `action_required` and needs maintainer approval to start. The one deselected test is the pre-existing Windows-only tilde expectation in `tests/agent/lsp/test_workspace.py::test_normalize_path_expands_tilde`, which is unrelated to these files. Real-process validation selected and initialized both canonical wrappers: ```text pyright -> .../node_modules/.bin/pyright-langserver.cmd running=true TypeScript -> .../node_modules/.bin/typescript-language-server.cmd running=true ``` Regression coverage includes native-wrapper preference, POSIX-only stale repair, canonical wrapper location, native PE launchers, metacharacter-containing paths and arguments, npm auto-install, Node health probes, pip `Scripts` discovery, non-Windows behavior, and direct `.cmd` LSP startup. ## Scope Changed files: - `agent/lsp/install.py` - `agent/lsp/client.py` - `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py` - `hermes_constants.py` - launcher-focused regression tests

After maintainer feedback, this branch was rebased onto current `upstream/main` and the redundant `agent/usage_pricing.py` plus `tests/agent/test_usage_pricing.py` hunks were removed. The remaining PR is limited to the still-uncovered raw stream payload normalization path in `agent/codex_runtime.py`. ## How to test ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh \ tests/run_agent/test_run_agent_codex_responses.py \ tests/run_agent/test_streaming.py \ tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py \ tests/agent/test_auxiliary_explicit_cancellation.py -q python3 -m py_compile agent/codex_runtime.py python3 scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --diff upstream/main git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD ``` Manual/raw-payload reproduction is encoded by `test_consume_codex_stream_normalizes_raw_dict_output_items`, which feeds raw dictionary SSE frames through `_consume_codex_event_stream()` and verifies the nested output text survives. ## Test results Post-rebase focused canonical run: - `274 passed` - `0 failed` - `4 skipped` - Windows footgun scan: passed - `py_compile`: passed - `git diff --check`: passed The first focused attempt exposed an environment/bootstrap issue—not a code failure—because the new worktree venv lacked the optional Anthropic SDK required by three unchanged sibling streaming tests. Installing the repository-pinned `anthropic==0.87.0` extra and rerunning the same canonical command produced the green result above. ## Platforms tested - WSL2 / Linux - Python 3.11.15 - Worktree-local `.venv` built from the current repository with dev dependencies and the pinned Anthropic optional dependency ## Cross-platform impact The functional change is pure Python data-shape normalization. It adds no filesystem, process, shell, path, or operating-system-specific behavior. `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py --diff upstream/main` reports no findings. ## Related upstream work - #85769 now covers the mapping-safe usage read that was part of this PR's earlier scope; that redundant code has been removed here. - Distinct from #63654, which fixes cached-token double counting in the separate Codex app-server accounting path. - Distinct from #61751, which unifies app-server turn finalization and lifecycle behavior.

signals.title: fix(daemon_pool): support CPython 3.14 ThreadPoolExecutor internals
signals.text: ## Symptom On CPython 3.14, every task that spins up a `DaemonThreadPoolExecutor` worker crashes with: ``` AttributeError: 'DaemonThreadPoolExecutor' object has no attribute '_initializer' ``` Because this pool backs concurrent tool execution, skill-catalog fan-out, background memory sync, and subagent timeout wrappers, the failure surfaces broadly at runtime — e.g. `skill_view` / concurrent tool batches intermittently returning `Error during OpenAI-compatible API call: 'DaemonThreadPoolExecutor' object has no attribute '_initializer'`. ## Root cause `tools/daemon_pool.py::DaemonThreadPoolExecutor._adjust_thread_count` mirrors CPython's private worker-spawn code (to set `daemon=True` and skip `_threads_queues` registration). It was written for the 3.8–3.13 internals. CPython **3.14 refactored those internals**: - `_worker` target signature changed from `(executor_ref, work_queue, initializer, initargs)` to `(executor_ref, ctx, work_queue)`, where `ctx = self._create_worker_context()`. - The `_initializer` / `_initargs` attributes were removed. So on 3.14 the old arg tuple references a now-nonexistent `self._initializer` → `AttributeError` on every worker spawn. Verified against the live 3.14 stdlib: ``` >>> [a for a in vars(ThreadPoolExecutor(1)) if 'init' in a.lower()] [] # no _initializer/_initargs >>> inspect.signature(concurrent.futures.thread._worker) (executor_reference, ctx, work_queue) ``` ## Fix Make `_adjust_thread_count` version-adaptive: detect the 3.14+ contract via `hasattr(self, "_create_worker_context")` and build the correct `_worker` args for each interpreter. The legacy branch uses `getattr` for `_initializer`/`_initargs` so it stays type-clean. Single class, both contracts, **no behavior change on 3.8–3.13**. This fixes the whole bug class (all consumers spawn workers through this one overridden method) rather than any single call site. ## Verification (Python 3.14.6, Termux/Android, against current `main` — `daemon_pool.py` is byte-identical to upstream) ``` $ python -m pytest tests/tools/test_daemon_pool.py -v tests/tools/test_daemon_pool.py::test_workers_are_daemon_threads PASSED tests/tools/test_daemon_pool.py::test_results_and_initializer_work_like_stdlib PASSED tests/tools/test_daemon_pool.py::test_idle_worker_reuse PASSED tests/tools/test_daemon_pool.py::test_wedged_worker_does_not_block_interpreter_exit PASSED 4 passed in 1.59s $ ruff check tools/daemon_pool.py All checks passed! ``` The existing `test_results_and_initializer_work_like_stdlib` exercises the initializer path (the one that crashed) and the wedged-worker test confirms the daemon/no-`_threads_queues` invariant still holds. ## Scope / footprint One file, one method. No new tools, no config, no env vars, no core-surface change; prompt caching and message alternation untouched.

Timeout policy must follow each destination, not the primary route. ## Review resolution The fallback timeout policy is now centralized in `_resolve_fallback_timeout()`. signals.title: fix: propagate clarify callback through plugin tool dispatch bridge
signals.text: ## Summary - propagate the platform `clarify_callback` through concurrent and sequential tool execution - preserve it across nested `tool_call` recursion and plugin registry dispatch - prevent model-supplied arguments from overriding the framework callback - retain the legacy direct-registry callback fallback and fail closed when no callback exists - add regression tests for nested plugin clarification ## Problem When a plugin-dispatched tool invokes `clarify` through the `tool_call` bridge, the platform callback is dropped. The nested call reaches the clarify handler without the callback and fails even though a valid callback exists on the originating agent. Reproduction path: 1. Register a plugin tool that dispatches `clarify` through `tool_call`. 2. Attach a working `clarify_callback` to the agent. 3. Invoke the plugin tool. 4. The nested clarification fails because the callback was not forwarded. ## Root cause `handle_function_call` and the executor/helper chain did not accept or propagate the agent's callback. Nested dispatch constructs a fresh context, so the callback was lost before the clarify registry handler ran. ## Solution - `agent_runtime_helpers.py` forwards the callback for concurrent tool invocation. - `tool_executor.py` forwards it from sequential quiet and non-quiet dispatch. - `model_tools.py` preserves it across `tool_call` recursion and into registry dispatch. - `clarify_tool.py` consumes the explicit callback with legacy fallback. The new parameter is optional, preserving existing callers. ## Security properties - The callback is sourced from framework state, not model-controlled function arguments. - Model arguments cannot inject or replace the framework callback. - Missing framework and legacy callbacks still fail closed. - The callback remains call-local; no process-global or shared mutable context is introduced. - No new IPC, serialization, or network surface is added. ## Tests Current candidate rebased onto upstream `cb47f59ffa`: - `tests/test_nested_plugin_clarify_callback.py` — **3 passed** - `tests/run_agent/test_run_agent.py -k "clarify"` — **4 passed** - implementation-phase coherent executor/timeout suite — **260 passed** on the immediately preceding reviewed base; the final four-commit upstream refresh replayed both PR commits byte-identically - upstream-delta send-target parsing — **11 passed** on the private mirror candidate - `git diff --check`, changed-module compilation, and candidate-local import-origin probes — passed - independent exact-candidate release gate — **PASS** The regression tests cover: - a real framework callback winning over model-spoofed callback arguments - failure when no framework callback exists despite spoofed arguments - recursive dispatch through the `tool_call` bridge preserving the callback - both sequential quiet-mode branches - concurrent registry dispatch preserving the exact platform callback The original July 24 candidate also completed the canonical full runner with **46,600 passed** and zero candidate-only final failures; its 23 final failures reproduced exactly on pristine upstream. This historical broad-suite result predates the current upstream rebase and is included for provenance, not presented as a current-base run. ## Related work - #12576 addresses gateway-created agent wiring and is non-equivalent. - #12814 adds an `on_clarify` notification hook once a callback is available; this PR fixes callback preservation before that point. Both touch `clarify_tool.py`, so normal conflict resolution may be needed if #12814 lands first. - #14602 adds CLI/plugin response hooks and is non-equivalent. - #29526 proposed a CLI-only `PluginContext.ask_user` overlay and is closed.

signals.title: fix(hermes_cli): stop planted cwd PowerShell from running during managed-uv bootstrap
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? On Windows, managed-uv bootstrap no longer spawns a bare `powershell` name. It resolves the absolute System32 Windows PowerShell host so an attacker-writable current directory cannot plant `powershell.exe` / `.cmd` / `.bat` and gain arbitrary code execution under `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` when Hermes installs missing managed uv. ### Bug Cause `_install_uv_windows` called `subprocess.run(["powershell", "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass", "-c", "irm ... | iex"], ...)`. On Windows, CreateProcess resolves extension-less names via PATHEXT and searches the process cwd before PATH, so a planted host wins. This path is reached from `ensure_uv()` when `$HERMES_HOME/bin/uv.exe` is missing (first bootstrap / deleted binary), including `hermes update` recovery. ### Reproduction Steps 1. Remove or rename `%USERPROFILE%\.hermes\bin\uv.exe` (or the active profile's `HERMES_HOME\bin\uv.exe`). 2. In an untrusted project directory, plant `powershell.cmd` or `powershell.exe` that only creates a marker file. 3. From that directory, run a command that calls `ensure_uv()` (for example `hermes update`). Expected: only `%SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe` is spawned. Before fix: the planted cwd host runs as the Hermes user before any Astral installer integrity check. ### Fix Add `_resolve_windows_powershell_host()` that returns the absolute System32 PowerShell path from `SystemRoot` / `WINDIR`, and raises `FileNotFoundError` if missing (no bare-name fallback). `_install_uv_windows` uses that path. Tests cover SystemRoot/WINDIR resolution, missing-host fail-closed, and a cwd decoy that must not win. ## Related Issue No issue ## Type of Change - [x] 🔒 Security fix ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/managed_uv.py` - resolve absolute System32 PowerShell for Windows managed-uv install; refuse bare-name fallback - `tests/hermes_cli/test_managed_uv.py` - lock host resolution and cwd-decoy behavior ## How to Test 1. Manual (Windows): remove managed `uv.exe`, plant a cwd `powershell` decoy, run a path that calls `ensure_uv()`, confirm only System32 PowerShell is used. 2. signals.title: fix(hermes_cli): stop unsigned skills-index from installing dangerous skills as builtin
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Skill install was granting builtin trust (which allows dangerous scan verdicts) whenever `bundle.source == "official"`, even when that string came from the unsigned hermes skills index or another non-optional adapter. This PR ties official/builtin install trust to the concrete local `OptionalSkillSource` adapter identity and sanitizes privileged provenance fields copied from index JSON. ### Bug Cause `do_install` (and the dashboard hub scan path) chose scan provenance from `bundle.source`. `HermesIndexSource.fetch` copies `entry.get("source")` from the unsigned HTTPS skills-index onto GitHub-fetched bundles. An index entry with `source="official"` (or identifier exactly `official` / `agent-created`) made `_resolve_trust_level` return `builtin`, and `INSTALL_POLICY["builtin"]` allows dangerous verdicts without `--force`. ### Reproduction Steps 1. Build a skill directory whose files trigger a dangerous skills-guard verdict (for example a `run.sh` with `curl ... | bash`). 2. Scan with `source="official"` and call `should_allow_install(..., force=False)`. 3. Repeat with `source="community"` (or a non-reserved hermes-index identity). Expected: dangerous skills from non-optional adapters are blocked. Before fix: `source="official"` returns allow (`Allowed (builtin source, dangerous verdict)`). ### Fix - Elevate to official/builtin scan provenance only when the matched adapter is `isinstance(..., OptionalSkillSource)`. - Scrub reserved scan identifiers (`official`, `agent-created`) on the non-optional fallback path. - Sanitize privileged `source` / `trust_level` stamped by `HermesIndexSource`. - Apply the same scan-source helper on the dashboard hub scan path in `hermes_cli/web_routers/skills.py`. - Scrub reserved identifiers when `do_audit` feeds lock entries into `scan_skill`. - Add regression tests covering stamped `source=official`, spoofed `source_id()=="official"`, lock-entry audit scrubbing, and dangerous install policy blocking via real `_resolve_trust_level` + `should_allow_install`. Normal `hermes skills install official/...` still resolves through OptionalSkillSource first and keeps builtin trust for real local optional skills. ## Related Issue No issue ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] Security fix - [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage) ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/skills_hub.py` - OptionalSkillSource-gated official trust, reserved identifier scrub for install/audit scans - `hermes_cli/web_routers/skills.py` - dashboard hub scan uses the same provenance helper - `tools/skills_hub.py` - HermesIndexSource sanitizes privileged source/trust from unsigned index JSON - `tests/hermes_cli/test_skills_hub.py` - provenance + dangerous-install policy regressions - `tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_admin_endpoints.py` - hub scan endpoint coverage with real trust resolution - `tests/tools/test_skills_hub.py` - index sanitization unit coverage ## How to Test 1. Manual: confirm `scan_skill(..., source="official")` + dangerous findings still allows under builtin policy, while install via a hermes-index-like adapter with stamped `source="official"` no longer passes `official` as scan source. 2. Automated: ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh \ tests/hermes_cli/test_skills_hub.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_dashboard_admin_endpoints.py \ tests/tools/test_skills_hub.py \ tests/tools/test_skills_guard.py \ -q ``` ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the Contributing Guide - [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits - [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix/feature - [x] I've run `scripts/run_tests.sh` on relevant tests and they pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation - N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys - N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows - N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact - N/A (trust logic is OS-agnostic) - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior - N/A

signals.title: fix(acp): tolerate a null final_response when a turn is cancelled
signals.text: ### What & why Cancelling a turn could kill the session with: ``` AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith' ``` surfaced to the client as a bare JSON-RPC "Internal error". JetBrains treats that as a non-recoverable session failure: it tears down the session and kills the agent process, so a cancel could destroy a session that was otherwise healthy. `result.get("final_response", "")` assumed the key is absent-or-string, but the conversation loop can return it present-and-`None` — the truncation path returns `partial_response or None` outright (`agent/conversation_loop.py`). A `.get` default only applies to a *missing* key, so the value stayed `None`. The rest of the codebase already treats it as optional — `turn_finalizer` uses `len(final_response) if final_response else 0`, which is why the turn log prints `response_len=0` instead of crashing. The ACP adapter was the outlier. Normalising at the single ingress point covers all five downstream uses. ### How to test `tests/acp/test_server.py::TestPrompt::test_prompt_survives_null_final_response` drives a cancelled turn returning `final_response: None`. It fails with `AttributeError` on an unmodified checkout and passes with the fix. ### Platforms Platform-independent. Full `tests/acp` suite run on Windows 11: 326 passed; 4 pre-existing failures (`test_approval_isolation`, `test_edit_approval`, `test_ping_suppression`) reproduce on an unmodified checkout. Reported as the secondary exception in #73693. ---

signals.title: fix(acp): shield the JSON-RPC stdin from every child process
signals.text: ### What & why Defence in depth for the class in #74241. Fixing individual call sites only covers code we own and remember to annotate — and the guard meant to enforce that has a blind spot for calls formatted as `subprocess.run(` + newline. In ACP mode fd 0 is the protocol pipe. A child that inherits it can either steal bytes from the transport or block on it and hang the turn. This re-homes the transport onto a private, non-inheritable duplicate at startup and points fd 0 at the null device, so every descendant inherits NUL. That also covers processes we don't control and can't annotate: - per-session MCP servers launched on the client's behalf (in JetBrains, the IDE's own stdio MCP server is a direct child of the agent); - third-party user plugins under `get_hermes_home()/plugins`. Windows needs the extra `SetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE, ...)`: it hands children the process-wide standard handle rather than fd 0, so `dup2` alone leaves the pipe reachable. Gated on `sys.platform == "win32"`; POSIX needs only the `dup2`, which is ordinary daemon hygiene. Fail-open: if stdin can't be duplicated (no real stdin under an embedded or test harness) it logs and continues unshielded rather than refusing to start. ### How to test `tests/acp/test_entry.py::test_shield_stdin_redirects_fd0_to_devnull` spawns a subprocess, calls the shield, and asserts (a) fd 0 reads EOF — what a grandchild would inherit — and (b) the transport still reads the original stream. Without the shield the same probe reads the protocol line off fd 0. ### Platforms Verified on Windows 11 with an overlapped named pipe as stdin (matching the JetBrains/Eel launcher). The POSIX path is `dup2`-only. Happy to drop this if you'd rather keep to per-call-site fixes — #74241 and #74242 stand alone and fix the reported bug without it.

signals.title: feat: non-blocking /compress — background LLM thread with input queuing
signals.text: ## Problem When the user runs `/compress`, the CLI becomes unresponsive until the LLM compression call completes. For large conversation histories this can take 10–30 seconds. During this time: - The TUI spinner shows, but the input composer is effectively blocked — the user can type but hitting Enter does nothing visible until compression finishes. - If the user submits input during compression, it is silently eaten (never processed). This creates a sharp friction point in long sessions where `/compress` is most needed. ## Solution Three small, targeted changes to `cli.py`: ### 1. Background thread (`_manual_compress`) The compression LLM call is moved from the synchronous `_busy_command` context manager into a `threading.Thread(target=..., daemon=True)`. The thread: - Sets `_compress_in_progress = True` (guard against concurrent invocations) - Sets `_command_blocks_input = False` so the TUI composer remains fully writable - Runs the existing compression logic **unchanged** - In a `finally` block: resets all state flags and drains any queued input into `_pending_input` ### 2. Input queuing (`handle_enter` → `_compress_pending`) If the user presses Enter while `_compress_in_progress` is `True`: - The input text (with attached images) is appended to `_compress_pending` deque - The buffer is reset and a placeholder hint "🗜️ Input queued — compress in progress" is printed - Normal input handling is **not** invoked — avoids race conditions with compression - After compression finishes, the `finally` block drains `_compress_pending` into `_pending_input`, which is then consumed by the normal `process_loop` ### 3. Concurrency guard If `/compress` is issued during an already-running compression, a warning is printed and the duplicate is dropped. ## Design decisions | Decision | Rationale | |----------|-----------| | `threading.Thread` (not `asyncio`) | The TUI loop is synchronous (`prompt_toolkit` event loop). Using `asyncio` would require refactoring the entire event handling pipeline. A daemon thread is the minimal, safe bolt-on. | | `deque` for pending input | `handle_enter` runs on the UI thread; appending to a deque is lock-free in CPython thanks to the GIL. No additional synchronization needed. | | `_busy_command` not used | `_busy_command` blocks the main thread (it `sleep`s). We bypass it entirely and set its internal state flags directly (`_command_running`, `_command_blocks_input`, `_command_status`). | | Compress logic unchanged | The `_run_compress()` inner function wraps the **exact same** LLM call, error handling, and compression result application. Only the threading boundary is new. | | No `Queue` for pending input | A `collections.deque` is sufficient — consumed in the `finally` block after the thread joins implicitly (daemon thread). No producer/consumer cross-thread coordination needed. | ## Changes - `cli.py`: 40 additions, 1 deletion - 3 insertion points: `__init__` (state vars), `_manual_compress` (threading), `handle_enter` (queuing) ## Testing - Manual testing: `/compress` in a session with ~200 messages — TUI composer stayed responsive, text typed during compression appeared as normal after completion. - AST parse and `py_compile` both pass on Python 3.11. - No changes to the compression logic itself — existing `/compress` behavior is preserved. ## Compatibility - No new dependencies (`threading`, `collections.deque` are stdlib). - No changes to public API or configuration. - All existing tests should continue to pass (no logic changes).

signals.title: fix(install): surface aborted gateway restart during hermes update (#78574)
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? `hermes update` can finish with a clean `✓ Update complete!` and exit 0 while leaving a running gateway on pre-update modules — the next turn then dies with `ImportError: cannot import name 'is_trivial_prompt' from 'agent.memory_provider'`. The cause is the blanket handler around the entire gateway auto-restart phase in `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py`: ```python except Exception as e: logger.debug("Gateway restart during update failed: %s", e) ``` If anything in that phase raises — most plausibly the `from hermes_cli.gateway import (...)` at the top of the block, which pulls the *freshly pulled* module into a process that already loaded the *pre-update* ones — the whole phase is skipped. Every `→ draining …` / `✓ Restarted hermes-gateway` line vanishes from the update log, and the failure is invisible at default log level. That matches the reported log exactly: earlier updates show drain/restart lines, the failing run shows none, and exit status is 0. Upstream already has the right machinery for the *partial* failure case (`failed_or_stale_units` → `_warn_incomplete_gateway_fleet_restart` → `gateway_fleet_restart_incomplete` → nonzero exit + `.update_exit_code` marker). This PR routes the *total* failure case into the same contract instead of swallowing it. On exception the handler now: 1. probes for surviving gateway PIDs (best-effort, never raises — a broken `hermes_cli.gateway` is itself one of the ways we get here); 2. unless it can *positively* prove nothing is running (empty list), prints the underlying exception, the surviving PIDs, and `hermes gateway restart`; 3. sets `gateway_fleet_restart_incomplete`, so the update exits nonzero and — under `--gateway` — writes `1` to `.update_exit_code`, exactly like the existing failed-unit path. `None` (undeterminable) and a non-empty PID list are both treated as "assume stale"; only a positive empty result stays quiet, so a host with no gateway running does not start failing its updates. This is deliberately a *reporting* fix, not an attempt to guess why the phase died: the issue asks for "exit nonzero or print a clear warning and manual recovery command", and any root cause behind that blanket `except` produces the same silent-stale outcome today. ## Related Issue Fixes #78574 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py` - new `_surviving_gateway_pids_after_failed_restart()` — best-effort probe for gateways still running after the restart phase aborted; returns `None` when undeterminable so callers can distinguish "nothing running" from "cannot tell". - new `_warn_gateway_restart_phase_aborted()` — prints the cause, the surviving PIDs, and the `hermes gateway restart` / `hermes gateway status` recovery commands. Mirrors the wording/shape of the neighbouring `_warn_incomplete_gateway_fleet_restart()`. - the phase-level `except Exception` now calls both, sets `gateway_fleet_restart_incomplete = True`, and writes the gateway-mode `.update_exit_code` marker. - `hermes_cli/main.py` — re-export the two new helpers alongside the existing update-path names. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_gateway_restart_aborted.py` — new regression tests. ## How to Test ``` scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update_gateway_restart_aborted.py tests/hermes_cli/test_update_fleet_restart_timeout.py ``` Result: `2 files, 9 tests passed, 0 failed`. Full update-path suite (22 files, includes every `tests/hermes_cli/test_update*.py` and `test_cmd_update*.py`): ``` scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_update*.py tests/hermes_cli/test_cmd_update*.py ``` Result: `22 files, 167 tests passed, 0 failed`. The tests cover the invariants from the issue: the probe never raises when `hermes_cli.gateway` is broken, an empty probe result stays distinguishable from an undeterminable one, and the warning names both the underlying cause and the manual recovery command. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass <!-- ran the 22-file update-path suite above, not the whole tree --> - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0) ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A <!-- N/A: helper docstrings only --> - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A <!-- N/A: no new config keys --> - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A <!-- N/A --> - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A <!-- the handler is platform-agnostic; `write_text` uses `encoding="utf-8"`; no new POSIX-only calls --> - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A <!-- N/A --> ## Screenshots / Logs Before (reported in #78574 — no drain/restart step, exit 0): ```text ✓ Update complete! Tip: You can now select a provider and model: hermes model ``` After, when the restart phase aborts: ```text ⚠ Update incomplete — gateway auto-restart failed: cannot import name 'is_trivial_prompt' from 'agent.memory_provider' Gateway process(es) still running pre-update code: 4321 Restart it manually, then verify: hermes gateway restart hermes gateway status ``` …and the update process exits nonzero.

signals.title: fix(undo): restore pre-compaction history across compaction boundaries
signals.text: ## Summary Fix #81130. `/undo` could not reverse an in-place compaction — it only flipped `active=0` on projection rows while archived source rows stayed invisible, so the agent either saw a truncated summary or lost its entire context. Three sub-fixes: 1. **Persist `display_kind="compression_summary"` on standalone summaries** so `list_recent_user_messages` never counts them as undo targets (the in-memory `_compressed_summary` marker did not survive the DB round-trip). 2. **Make `rewind_to_message` compaction-aware** via two new nullable columns on the `messages` table (`compaction_group`, `source_message_id`). `archive_and_compact` records which source row each projection row was copied from; `rewind_to_message` follows that edge to retire the projection, restore the archived source snapshot, and truncate at the mapped source position — all in one write txn. Counters are recomputed from the resulting active set. Sessions without lineage metadata (pre-v26) fall through to the original suffix-delete path unchanged. 3. **CLI `undo_last` reloads `conversation_history` from DB** when a compaction boundary is crossed, matching the TUI's existing full-rebuild pattern. Gateway and TUI need no code changes. ## Test plan - 13 new tests in `TestRewindCompactionAware`: single/multi-compaction undo, summary filtering, post-compaction turn suffix delete, counter recompute, idempotency, legacy session fallback, duplicate user content mapping - 223 existing tests pass (including `test_in_place_compaction`, `test_undo_command`, `test_undo_rewind_session`, `test_compressed_summary_metadata`) — zero regressions

signals.title: feat(agent): add adaptive per-turn reasoning
signals.text: ## Summary - add opt-in `agent.adaptive_reasoning` with deterministic, per-turn effort selection and no extra classifier-model request - keep ordinary or ambiguous work at the configured baseline, conservatively downshift positively simple turns to `low` when `min_effort: low` is enabled, and raise complex work to `high` or `xhigh` - apply the selected level for the complete tool loop, restore the baseline afterward, and show a deduplicated user-facing notice when the level changes - preserve explicit CLI/session/Desktop choices and provider/model effort clamps - keep state isolated per conversation; delegated children inherit the parent turn's effective level and independently reclassify their own goal unless explicitly pinned with `delegation.reasoning_effort` ## Design Classification is local and deterministic. It uses bounded signal categories and structural evidence rather than another LLM call, so normal turns do not pay an additional network request, token charge, OAuth path, or classification latency. Downshift is deliberately conservative: `low` requires positive evidence of a casual message, short factual request, or single read-only mechanical step, with no code, error, compound, multi-question, multi-step, or consequential-work signal. Uncertain inputs remain at the configured baseline. An explicit `agent.reasoning_effort` baseline is required. Adaptive adjustment is inert when thinking is unset or explicitly disabled. ## Why adaptive mode does not disable reasoning This change intentionally never selects `none` or toggles thinking off for individual turns. On providers such as Anthropic, thinking presence participates in the message-cache namespace; switching it on and off inside a conversation fragments that cache and can multiply input cost. Keeping thinking present while varying only its level preserves one namespace on current adaptive-thinking models. Legacy budget-token models may still re-key their message cache when the budget changes, but system/tool caches remain reusable. `low` captures the useful latency/cost reduction for simple turns without changing thinking presence or silently re-enabling reasoning that the user disabled. ## Issue alignment Addresses #40306 and its duplicate #74725. This does **not** use `Closes`, because those issues also propose per-turn `none` and an integrated reasoning display; both are intentionally outside this PR. Maintainers can decide whether conservative `low` is sufficient or whether the remaining UX belongs in a follow-up. Related prior art: open #61410 also uses deterministic local heuristics; its current revision has unresolved review gaps in gateway and provider-specific paths. This PR independently takes a broader session/tool-loop approach, including restoration, explicit overrides, Desktop semantics, and delegated children. Closed #58305 explored a per-request classifier-model call. ## Validation Current candidate on upstream `cb47f59ffa`: - adaptive policy, CLI configuration, delegation, and TUI gateway suites — **707 passed, 0 failed** - `git diff --check`, changed-module compilation, and candidate-local import-origin probes — passed - the adaptive patch is content-identical to the previous PR head; only parent context, blob ids, and hunk offsets changed - `run_conversation` begins adaptive reasoning after the durable-turn-lease helpers introduced by #84234, while baseline restoration remains the final statement of the outer `finally` - rebased as one bisectable commit (`6d97b094fd`) - independent exact-candidate release gate — **PASS** The previous broader candidate validation remains historical provenance; the counts above are the checks run against the current rebased bytes.
