signal.title: fix(config): stop runtime CWD values from triggering dotenv warnings
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Stops Hermes from reporting `TERMINAL_CWD` or `MESSAGING_CWD` as deprecated `.env` settings when those values exist only in the process environment. Gateway starts and resumed sessions no longer show a false migration warning, while real deprecated entries on disk continue to produce the warning. ### Symptom Starting the gateway with a runtime-populated `TERMINAL_CWD` prints a warning claiming that the value was found in `.env`, even when `.env` contains no active entry. ### Impact Affected users see an incorrect deprecation warning on every gateway start and are instructed to remove a setting that is not present in their `.env` file. This obscures legitimate migration warnings and makes normal config bridges or session restoration appear misconfigured. ### Bug Cause **Trigger:** `hermes_cli/config.py` / `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` reading `os.environ` **Causal chain:** 1. Runtime config bridging or session restoration places `TERMINAL_CWD` in the process environment. 2. `warn_deprecated_cwd_env_vars()` reads the merged process environment instead of the `.env` file it claims to diagnose. 3. Hermes reports the runtime-only value as a deprecated `.env` entry. **Why it is wrong:** Process environment provenance cannot distinguish a user-authored `.env` entry from legitimate runtime state, so the warning attributes values to the wrong source. **Working sibling / contrast:** The doctor diagnostic already checks parsed `.env` contents rather than process environment values, which avoids this false positive. **Ruled out:** A commented `# TERMINAL_CWD=.` line is not parsed as an active setting; regression coverage confirms commented and empty values remain silent. ### Fix Read deprecated CWD settings through the existing `.env` parser, trim empty values, and warn for every real deprecated disk entry regardless of the current `terminal.cwd` config. Regression tests cover process-only values, both deprecated disk entries, explicit config combined with a legacy disk entry, and commented or empty values. ## Related Issue Fixes #85695 ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/config.py` - inspect parsed `.env` values instead of `os.environ` when emitting CWD migration warnings. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py` - add provenance and legacy-entry behavior coverage. ## How to Test 1. Put only a commented `# TERMINAL_CWD=.` entry in `.env`, set `TERMINAL_CWD` in the process environment, and confirm no deprecation warning is emitted. 2. Add an active `TERMINAL_CWD=/legacy/path` entry to `.env` and confirm the migration warning is emitted, including when `terminal.cwd` is explicitly configured. 3. Automated (already run locally, 56 passed): ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_deprecated_cwd_warning.py tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor.py ``` ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Relevant documentation update: N/A - no user-facing configuration contract changed - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` update: N/A - no config keys changed - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` update: N/A - no architecture or workflow changed - [x] Cross-platform impact considered - `.env` parsing is shared across supported platforms - [x] Tool descriptions/schemas update: N/A - no model tool behavior changed ## Screenshots / Logs Targeted test suite: 56 passed.

signal.title: [UX] Enable mouse support (cursor positioning, scrolling) with config toggle
signal.text: ## Summary Mouse support is explicitly disabled in the prompt_toolkit Application: `cli.py:1755`: ```python mouse_support=False, ``` This means users cannot: - Click to position the cursor in the input area - Select text with the mouse - Scroll with the mouse wheel (within prompt_toolkit) ## Suggested fix 1. Flip to `mouse_support=True` as the default 2. Add a `tui.mouse_support` config toggle as an escape hatch for terminals where mouse capture causes issues (tmux, screen, some SSH setups) ```python mouse_support=self.config.get("tui", {}).get("mouse_support", True), ``` ## Risk Low. Some terminal multiplexers (tmux, screen) may behave oddly with mouse capture enabled. The config toggle provides an escape hatch. Most modern terminals handle this fine. ## Impact - **Severity**: High — basic expected interaction pattern - **Effort**: Tiny — one boolean flip + optional config key ## Ref UX audit item #10.

signal.title: [Bug]: Desktop retry of a failed turn silently truncates history via ordinal-only path — row-id guard (#83785) does not cover it
signal.text: ## Bug Description With #83785 merged, deliberate edits/rewinds are protected by durable `truncate_before_row_id` addressing + 4018/4030 refusals. But the **retry / plain-resubmit path after a failed turn** still travels the ordinal-only back-compat path, and a stale ordinal mis-aimed a real truncation in production: a retry of a 429-failed turn silently discarded 68 messages (4 user-turns deeper than intended) from the model's context. This is the residual hole of #82959 (auto-closed by the #83785 merge): the client and server ordinal address spaces had diverged, and because no row id was attached on this path, neither cross-check could fire. ## Incident (2026-08-14, Windows Desktop, kimi-k3 long session with prior in-place compactions) 1. `23:49:36` — user submits a normal new message; agent turn starts. 2. `23:50:21–23:50:47` — turn dies on HTTP 429 after 3 retries (`API call failed after 3 retries ... msgs=602`). 3. `23:53:37` — user re-attempts the failed turn. Gateway log: `prompt.submit: truncating session … history 600 -> 532 messages (ordinal=19)`. 4. **No new user text was persisted with that submit** (verified in `state.db`: the only rows stamped `23:53:37` are rebuild copies of earlier messages). 5. The cut deactivated 68 rows starting from a user message sent at **22:56** — four user-turns *before* the message being retried — silently dropping 3 subsequent user messages plus ~48 min of agent work from the model's active context. 6. The Desktop transcript still shows all discarded messages in original order (renderer state), so from the user's side the history looked intact; the model later discovered side effects (files, wiki edits, background processes) it had no memory of — a confusing divergence. Data was fully recoverable thanks to `archive_dropped` from #82950 — that safeguard worked exactly as intended. ## Expected Behavior Any submit that truncates should be addressed durably (row id) regardless of which client path initiates it (edit / regenerate / retry-after-error / plain resubmit with leaked composer state). If a row id can't be supplied, the gateway should refuse rather than trust an ordinal whose address space may have drifted from the renderer's. ## Analysis - The ordinal the client sent (`19`) was presumably correct in the renderer's *visible* user-message list, but the gateway counts all `role==user` non-`display_kind` rows — after in-place compactions, rebuild copies, and branch hiding, the two lists no longer align, so ordinal 19 resolved to different messages on each side. Exactly the drift #82959 catalogued. - `planEdit` (use-prompt-actions) attaches `source.rowId` for edits, and the failed-turn case (`isFailedTurn`) deliberately sends **no** truncation — but the observed submit did truncate with an ordinal and no row id, so it came from a path where the truncate state wasn't cleared and no durable id was attached (retry/resubmit with leaked composer rewind state, matching the #82756 mechanism). - Suggestions: (a) thread `rowId` through retry/resubmit/regenerate paths too; (b) clear composer truncate state when a turn fails; (c) gateway-side strict mode: refuse ordinal-only truncation (`4004`) for sessions whose history carries row ids.

signal.title: Kanban project worktrees start from stale local HEAD instead of fetched origin/main
signal.text: ## Bug New project-linked Kanban task worktrees are created from the primary checkout's incidental `HEAD`, even when local `main` is stale/diverged from protected `origin/main`. ## Exact evidence - `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::_ensure_git_worktree` uses: `git -C <repo> worktree add -b <task-branch> <target> HEAD` - Project repo local `main`: `acd76b8dcdf23e963bc7105e042d414850331c99` - Protected `origin/main`: `8bf26916260358e731910bcf1b6d93d72b604a58` - Newly created project tasks `t_b725d07a` and `t_37018d67` both started at the stale local SHA. Their clean worktrees required incident recovery to the protected remote tip. ## Expected invariant For a new project-linked task branch, fetch `origin` first and base the branch on fetched `origin/main` (or the fetched symbolic remote default for non-main repositories). Existing task branches must be reused unchanged so retries remain idempotent and in-flight work is never discarded. Local-only repositories may retain `HEAD` fallback. ## Reproduction A regression test creates a repository with a bare `origin`, advances remote `main`, independently advances local `main`, calls `_ensure_git_worktree`, and compares the new worktree HEAD to `origin/main`. Current upstream behavior fails because the new branch equals local `main`. ## Validated patch A local patch introduces `_worktree_base_ref`, fetches/prunes `origin`, prefers verified `refs/remotes/origin/main^{commit}`, falls back to the fetched symbolic remote default, and uses that ref only for new branches. Targeted result: 10 tests passed across worktree isolation, project linking, and board-project scoping; Ruff and `git diff --check` pass. Local patch commit: `149221ff8b8fd233b8824cde3fc73b30a3250294` (not published).

signal.title: [Feature]: Route file:// links / raw local paths through #media: in Desktop chat (currently rendered as [blocked])
signal.text: ### Environment Windows 11, Hermes Desktop app (packaged build), streamdown 2.5.0 / @assistant-ui/react-streamdown 0.3.5 ### Problem When the agent emits a markdown link pointing at a local file, e.g. ```markdown [open the report](file:///C:/Users/PC/Desktop/report.md) ``` the chat renders it as `open the report [blocked]` — the link is replaced by the text `[blocked]` and is not clickable at all. Root cause: `harden-react-markdown` (bundled inside streamdown) hard-blocks the `file:` protocol. Its allowlist is `https/http/irc/ircs/mailto/xmpp/blob` and its deny set includes `file:`, `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`. Per the package's own Security Note, `file:` is always blocked even with `allowedProtocols={['*']}` — there is no configuration escape hatch. This is a UX dead-end for a desktop app whose whole point is dealing with local files: the main process already knows how to open local files (`electron/main.ts` `openExternalUrl` → `shell.openPath`), so the capability exists — only the render layer kills the link before it can be clicked. ### Related - #38786 — generated local images rendered as `[Image blocked: ...]`; fixed by routing raw local paths through the `#media:<encoded-path>` protocol. Same root cause, same fix pattern. ### Expected behavior A `file://` link (or a raw Windows local path such as `C:\Users\...`) emitted by the agent should render as a clickable link/card that opens the local file with the OS default app via `shell.openPath` — e.g. by auto-converting it to `#media:<encodeURIComponent(path)>` in the markdown preprocess step, or by letting the markdown link component handle the `file:` protocol through the media path. ### Additional findings from debugging this (for whoever implements it) `#media:` already works end-user-side, with two format traps: 1. The href must start with `#media:` exactly. A leading slash (`/#media:...`) does not match `mediaPathFromMarkdownHref` (`startsWith('#media:')`), silently degrades to a plain link, and clicking it turns into SPA navigation — desktop.log then shows `Error invoking remote method 'hermes:openExternal': Error: Invalid external URL (file:///...index.html#/...)`. Users perceive this as "opens C:\ root". 2. The encoded path should be forward-slash form `/C:/Users/...` so `mediaExternalUrl` concatenates a valid `file:///C:/...` URL. Backslash form produces an invalid `file://C:\...` URL. Also: when `shell.openPath` fails (e.g. file extension association hijacked by a third-party app), the fallback `showItemInFolder` reveals the drive root rather than the file's folder, which is confusing. A clearer fallback (or an error toast naming the file) would help. This is a UX enhancement — `#media:` links hand-authored today work; the request is for `file://` links to work (or degrade gracefully) instead of rendering `[blocked]`.

signal.title: fix(terminal-tool): classify timeout exceptions as non-retriable, return 124
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? `terminal_tool` currently classifies timeout exceptions from local/SSH/container backends as transient errors and retries the command up to three times. This is wrong: a timeout means the command hit its wall-clock limit, not that the environment is flaky. Retrying can make a single timeout take ~14 seconds and produce duplicate output or side effects. The fix introduces `_is_timeout_error()` to reliably recognize timeout exceptions regardless of backend: - `TimeoutError` / `asyncio.TimeoutError` / `concurrent.futures.TimeoutError` (their `str()` is empty, so the old string check missed them) - `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` - third-party backends that include "timed out" or "timeout" in the message When a timeout is detected, `terminal_tool` immediately returns exit code `124` with an explicit timeout message and does not retry. ## Related Issue Fixes #86481 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `tools/terminal_tool.py`: add `_is_timeout_error()` helper and use it in the execution retry loop instead of the fragile `"timeout" in str(e).lower()` string check. - `tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py`: add unit tests for `_is_timeout_error()` and integration tests proving `terminal_tool()` returns `exit_code: 124` without retrying on `TimeoutError` and `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`. ## How to Test 1. `PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py -x -q` — all 16 tests pass. 2. Before the fix, the new `test_terminal_tool_timeout_error_returns_124_without_retry` fails: a `TimeoutError()` is retried and ultimately returns `exit_code: -1`. 3. After the fix, the same test passes: `exit_code: 124` with `Command timed out after 5 seconds`. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run `pytest tests/tools/test_terminal_tool.py -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS (Darwin 24.6.0) / Python 3.11.15 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — N/A - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

signal.title: [Bug]: Windows cron script execution uses base Python with PYTHONPATH, ignoring .pth files from editable installs
signal.text: ### Bug Description `cron/scheduler.py::_run_job_script` runs script jobs using `sys.executable`. On Windows environments where a virtual environment was created with `uv`, `_windows_cron_python_invocation` (around line 2162 of `cron/scheduler.py`) bypasses the venv launcher, invokes the base Python interpreter directly, and attempts to re-attach the venv by setting `PYTHONPATH` to its `site-packages`. However, `PYTHONPATH` entries are standard directory additions on `sys.path`. Python's site initialization does NOT process `.pth` files for paths added solely via `PYTHONPATH` — that only occurs for genuine site directories via `site.addsitedir()`. As a result, every editable package installed in the virtualenv (`pip install -e ...` / `.pth` links) is invisible to cron script jobs, resulting in `ModuleNotFoundError`. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Create a `uv` virtualenv on Windows. 2. Install a package in editable mode (`pip install -e <path>`). 3. Configure a cron script job (`no_agent: true` or python script) that imports the editable package. 4. Execute the cron job via the scheduler. ### Actual Behavior Under the base interpreter + scheduler's `PYTHONPATH`: - Standard non-editable packages (e.g. `yaml`): OK - Root on `PYTHONPATH` (`hermes_cli`): OK - Editable packages: `ModuleNotFoundError` ### Expected Behavior Editable packages installed in the virtual environment should be importable by scheduled cron scripts. ### Root Cause Analysis In `cron/scheduler.py`: `_windows_cron_python_invocation` sets `PYTHONPATH` but does not invoke `site.addsitedir()` on the venv site-packages. ### Proposed Fix In the script execution runner or Python invocation wrapper, ensure `site.addsitedir()` is called for the virtualenv's `site-packages` directory before script execution, ensuring `.pth` files are processed. ### Affected Component - Gateway / Cron / Tools - Operating System: Windows

signal.title: [Bug]: approvals.deny rules can be bypassed via repeated whitespace or tab characters
signal.text: ### Bug Description `tools/approval.py::_match_user_deny_rule` matches `approvals.deny` glob patterns against command strings using `fnmatch.fnmatchcase`. The command deobfuscation pipeline collapses quote-splitting, backslash escapes, ANSI sequences, and Unicode tricks, but it does **not** collapse repeated whitespace or tab characters. Because `fnmatch` cannot represent "one or more whitespace characters", any deny glob written with literal spaces between arguments (e.g. `git push --force origin main` or `gh repo delete <repo>`) can be completely bypassed by inserting an additional space or a tab. Since `approvals.deny` is designed as the tier-1 un-bypassable floor (evaluated ahead of `--yolo`, `/yolo`, and `approvals.mode=off`), this allows dangerous or irreversible commands to execute without approval if separated by whitespace variations. ### Steps to Reproduce / Measured Variants Evaluate against a standard 6-glob deny list with single spaces: - `git push --force origin main` -> BLOCKED (canonical control) - `git push --force origin main` (double space) -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `git\tpush --force origin main` (tab) -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `git push -f origin main` -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `git push --force origin main` -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `git\tpush\t-f origin main` -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `gh repo delete someorg/somerepo` -> **NOT BLOCKED** - `GIT PUSH --FORCE origin main` -> **NOT BLOCKED** - ` git push --force origin main` (leading whitespace) -> **NOT BLOCKED** 8 of 11 tested whitespace variants bypassed the single-space deny globs. `detect_hardline_command` also returned `False` for all of these variants. ### Expected Behavior Commands matching deny patterns should be blocked regardless of whether arguments are separated by single spaces, multiple spaces, or tabs. ### Root Cause Analysis `_match_user_deny_rule` in `tools/approval.py` runs `fnmatch` directly on the deobfuscated string without whitespace normalization. ### Proposed Fix Collapse contiguous whitespace characters before running `fnmatch`, e.g.: ```python candidate_normalized = " ".join(candidate.split()) ``` (This pattern is already used in `terminal_tool.py:2097`). Additionally, document that deny globs are evaluated against whitespace-collapsed strings so rules do not intentionally include multi-space strings. ### Affected Component - Tools / Approvals / Security

signal.title: [Bug]: Gateway detachment diagnostics on Windows: stdin_is_tty is misleading and breakaway fallback is silent
signal.text: ### Bug Description While investigating gateway supervisor lifecycles on Windows, two detachment diagnostics and lifecycle issues were identified: 1. **`stdin_is_tty` in `gateway-exit-diag.log` is a misleading detachment diagnostic on Windows.** `gateway.py:4942` records `_stdin_is_tty = bool(sys.stdin and sys.stdin.isatty())` into every `gateway.start` record. On Windows, `os.isatty()` returns `True` for any character device, and `NUL` / `subprocess.DEVNULL` is a character device. A properly detached child process spawned with `windows_detach_flags()` (`0x09000200`) and `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` reports `stdin_is_tty: True` even though it has no attached console (`GetConsoleWindow() == 0`). The field only differentiates `pythonw.exe` (`sys.stdin is None` -> `False`) from `python.exe` (`True`), giving a misleading impression that a detached background gateway process remains attached to a terminal. 2. **Silent breakaway fallback in `_spawn_detached` leaves the gateway attached to launcher Job Objects.** In `gateway_windows.py:952-969`, if spawning with `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` fails with `OSError`, the spawn is retried with `windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()`. While falling back is reasonable, nothing is logged and no indicator is recorded in `gateway.start`. When launched from environments that use Windows Job Objects (e.g. Electron desktop app, Tauri installer, certain terminal emulators), the gateway silently remains in the parent job object. When the parent job owner exits, the gateway is terminated immediately by Windows with no exit record written to `gateway-exit-diag.log`. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. **For `stdin_is_tty`:** Spawn a child with `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | DETACHED_PROCESS` and `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL`. Inspect `sys.stdin.isatty()` — it returns `True`. 2. **For Breakaway Fallback:** Launch the gateway inside a nested job object that forbids breakaway. Observe that fallback occurs with 0 log messages and no metadata indicating breakaway failed. ### Expected Behavior - Diagnostics should accurately report whether a console/TTY is attached on Windows (e.g. via `GetConsoleWindow` or checking `HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED`). - Breakaway fallback should log a `WARNING` and record whether `breakaway` succeeded in the `gateway.start` record. ### Proposed Fix - In `gateway.py`: Replace raw `isatty()` on Windows with a check using `ctypes.windll.kernel32.GetConsoleWindow()` or `msvcrt`, and record `HERMES_GATEWAY_DETACHED`. - In `gateway_windows.py`: Log a warning when falling back to `windows_detach_flags_without_breakaway()`, and add a `breakaway: true/false` field to the startup diagnostic payload. ### Affected Component - Gateway / CLI - Platform: Windows

signal.title: [Bug]: Local model server connection errors fall through to unhelpful generic chat reply
signal.text: ### Bug Description `_gateway_provider_error_reply` (`gateway/run.py:522-536`) maps upstream model provider failures to concise, user-friendly chat responses across gateway channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, etc.). It currently contains dedicated branches for: - Authentication failures - Provider policy rejections - Rate limiting (429) All other errors fall through to the generic catch-all at line 536: > *"The model provider failed after retries. I kept raw provider details out of chat, check gateway logs for diagnostics."* For local/self-hosted model deployments (e.g. `llama.cpp`, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio running locally on `http://127.0.0.1:8033/v1`), the most common failure mode is that the local model server is simply not running or crashed. In this scenario, direct network connection errors (`httpx.ConnectError`, `openai.APIConnectionError`, `WinError 10061: target machine actively refused it`) are caught and properly classified in the core conversation loop, but are collapsed into the generic catch-all at the gateway reply layer. Directing a user on a mobile chat channel (away from the machine) to "check gateway logs for diagnostics" provides no actionable feedback when the server is just offline. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure Hermes with a local model endpoint (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8033/v1`). 2. Stop the local model server process. 3. Send a message to the agent via a gateway channel or a2a. ### Actual Behavior After retries, the user receives: > *"The model provider failed after retries. I kept raw provider details out of chat, check gateway logs for diagnostics."* Underlying error in conversation loop: `APIConnectionError` / `ConnectError` (WinError 10061). ### Expected Behavior The chat reply should clearly notify the user that the model endpoint is unreachable / not running. ### Proposed Fix Add a dedicated branch in `_gateway_provider_error_reply` before the catch-all for connection errors (`openai.APIConnectionError`, `httpx.ConnectError`, etc.): ```python if is_connection_error: return f"The model server at {configured_base_url} is not responding — it looks like it is not running." ``` ### Affected Component - Gateway - Agent Core / Configuration

signal.title: [Bug][Windows] TUI mouse wheel and selection fail under Windows Terminal/ConPTY
signal.text: ## Environment - OS: Windows 11 - Terminal: Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0 - Hermes Agent: v0.19.0 - Runtime path: native Windows / ConPTY - Config: `display.mouse_tracking: buttons` - No `HERMES_TUI_MOUSE_TRACKING`, `HERMES_TUI_DISABLE_MOUSE`, or `HERMES_TUI_INLINE` override initially ## Bug When running `hermes --tui` in Windows Terminal: - `PgUp/PgDn` scroll the transcript normally. - The mouse wheel does not scroll at all. - Mouse dragging cannot create a selectable/copyable text selection. - Enabling Windows Terminal `copyOnSelect` does not help because no selection is created. ## Reproduction 1. Open a native Windows Terminal tab. 2. Run `hermes --tui` with `display.mouse_tracking: buttons`. 3. Produce enough output to make the transcript scrollable. 4. Try the mouse wheel and drag over transcript text. ## Evidence A raw Node stdin probe enabled DECSET `1000`, `1002`, `1003`, and `1006` and ran for 90 seconds. Normal keyboard input (`a`, `b`, `c`, Enter) arrived, but zero mouse sequences arrived while testing wheel and drag input. This indicates that the failure occurs in the Windows Terminal/ConPTY mouse-event delivery path rather than in Hermes transcript scrolling itself. ## Workaround The following workaround restores native terminal scrollback, mouse selection, and copying on the same machine: ```powershell [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('HERMES_TUI_INLINE', '1', 'User') ``` After fully restarting Windows Terminal and launching `hermes --tui`, mouse scrolling and selection work. ## Expected behavior The TUI should either receive mouse events reliably under Windows Terminal/ConPTY, or provide a documented/fallback mode that preserves mouse wheel scrolling and native text selection/copying. Related: #4064, #83651
